tasks.n: Cup and kettle into sink basins
tasks.t: A Franka Panda arm on a wheeled Omron base with a liftable torso must put a glass cup into the left basin of a kitchen sink and a kettle into the right basin. The sides are fixed by the sink, so the robot has to keep track of which item goes where, and a glass and a kettle differ so much in shape that each needs its own grasp.

tasks.n: Fetch soap and brush from cabinet
tasks.t: A Franka Panda arm on a wheeled Omron base with a liftable torso must open a closed kitchen cabinet and move a bar of soap and a dish brush from inside it onto the counter. The items are hidden until the door is opened, so the robot has to open first, look, and only then fetch two different items one after the other.

tasks.n: Set shrimp and condiment on board
tasks.t: A Franka Panda arm on a wheeled Omron base with a liftable torso must move shrimp from a plate onto a cutting board, then take a condiment bottle out of an open cabinet and set it beside the board. The two-part sequence mixes two kinds of placement, on top of a surface and next to an object, and the bottle has to be fetched from inside a cabinet.

tasks.n: Reheat a meal in the microwave
tasks.t: A Franka Panda arm on a wheeled Omron base with a liftable torso must take a tupperware holding a shrimp and carrot meal from the open fridge, put it in the microwave, close the door and press start. The order is strict because start has no effect while the door is open, and the robot must carry the container across the kitchen and then handle both a door and a button.
st: tupperware with shrimp and carrot meal

tasks.n: Fetch fish from the fridge
tasks.t: A Franka Panda arm on a wheeled Omron base with a liftable torso must take a fish out of an open fridge and put it on a cutting board that lies some distance away across the kitchen. The pick-and-place itself is simple, but the base must drive to a good spot for each end of the transfer while the fish is being carried.

tasks.n: Stage spray bottle and brush by board
tasks.t: A Franka Panda arm on a wheeled Omron base with a liftable torso must prepare a sanitizing area by moving a spray bottle from a cabinet and a dish brush from the countertop beside the sink to the side of a cutting board. The items start in different places, so the robot has to fetch each from its own location and end with both close to the board.

tasks.n: Scrub a bowl with a sponge
tasks.t: A Franka Panda arm on a wheeled Omron base with a liftable torso must pick up a sponge and use it to scrub a bowl sitting in a kitchen sink. Touching the bowl is not enough: the sponge has to stay pressed against it while it moves over the surface, so the task tests holding a soft tool and keeping steady contact.

tasks.n: Sear a drumstick on the stove
tasks.t: A Franka Panda arm on a wheeled Omron base with a liftable torso must take a pan out of a cabinet, set it on the rear right burner, put a chicken drumstick on the stove in the pan and switch the burner on. The steps depend on each other, since the pan must be on the burner before the drumstick goes in, and the drumstick starts a fair distance from the stove.

tasks.n: Move condiments out of cabinet
tasks.t: A Franka Panda arm on a wheeled Omron base with a liftable torso must open a closed kitchen cabinet and carry a condiment bottle and a bottle of ketchup to the dining counter. The bottles are hidden until the cabinet is open, and the dining counter lies behind the robot, so it must turn its base around and drive over before placing both.

tasks.n: Set up a cutting station
tasks.t: A Franka Panda arm on a wheeled Omron base with a liftable torso must take a knife out of an open drawer and put it on a cutting board, then move a piece of meat from a plate onto the same board. The board sits at another part of the kitchen island, so the base has to relocate, and the robot handles a sharp tool and a food item in one job.

tasks.n: Stock breakfast items in cabinets
tasks.t: A Franka Panda arm on a wheeled Omron base with a liftable torso must take a canned food and a snack bar from the kitchen counter and put each one into the cabinet closest to it. The two items sit far apart along a long counter, so the base must travel between them, and the robot has to work out which cabinet is nearest to each instead of using a single storage spot.

tasks.n: Sweeten a cup of coffee
tasks.t: A Franka Panda arm on a wheeled Omron base with a liftable torso must drop a sugar cube from a saucer into a cup of coffee, then fetch milk from the fridge and put it down next to the coffee. The fridge is behind the robot, so the base has to turn and drive, and the two stages mix a tiny item placed into a cup with a larger item carried over.

tasks.n: Thaw an orange in the sink
tasks.t: A Franka Panda arm on a wheeled Omron base with a liftable torso must move an orange from the kitchen counter into the sink and then turn on the faucet. After the pick-and-place, the faucet handle has to be moved far enough into its water-on position, which calls for a different motion from grasping and carrying.

tasks.n: Fetch tongs from the drawer
tasks.t: A Franka Panda arm on a wheeled Omron base with a liftable torso must open a closed drawer on its left, take out a pair of tongs and place them on the dining counter beside a tray holding a hot dog. The tongs are hidden until the drawer is open, and the dining counter is behind the robot, so the base must turn around to finish the job.

tasks.n: Turn on the rear left burner
tasks.t: A Franka Panda arm on a wheeled Omron base with a liftable torso must switch on the rear left burner of a kitchen stove by turning its knob away from off. The stove has several burners, so the robot has to pick out the knob that belongs to the rear left one and twist it far enough for the burner to count as on.

tasks.n: Store water bottle and close cabinet
tasks.t: A fixed-base Fourier GR1 humanoid with two dexterous hands, standing at a kitchen counter in simulation, must pick up a bottle of water, put it inside a cabinet and then shut the cabinet door. The task chains a grasp, a placement into an enclosed space and a door-closing push, and the door must end fully closed with the bottle left inside.

tasks.n: Store can in drawer and close it
tasks.t: A fixed-base Fourier GR1 humanoid with two dexterous hands, working at a kitchen counter in simulation, must pick up a can, put it into an open drawer and push the drawer shut. The can has to end up inside while the drawer finishes fully closed, so the humanoid must release cleanly and then use an arm to slide the drawer in.

tasks.n: Store cup in drawer and close it
tasks.t: A fixed-base Fourier GR1 humanoid with two dexterous hands, standing at a kitchen counter in simulation, must pick up a cup, place it inside an open drawer and then close the drawer. It combines a grasp and a placement into a confined space with a final push, and the drawer must end fully shut with the cup inside.

tasks.n: Put milk in microwave and close it
tasks.t: A fixed-base Fourier GR1 humanoid with two dexterous hands, working at a kitchen counter in simulation, must pick up a milk container, place it inside an open microwave and shut the microwave door. The milk has to be left inside while the door ends fully closed, so the humanoid must set the item down and then push the hinged door with an arm.

tasks.n: Put potato in microwave and close it
tasks.t: A fixed-base Fourier GR1 humanoid with two dexterous hands, at a kitchen counter in simulation, must pick up a potato, set it inside an open microwave and then close the microwave door. It is a two-stage sequence of grasp-and-place followed by a door push, and the door must finish fully shut with the potato inside.

tasks.n: Store wine bottle and close cabinet
tasks.t: A fixed-base Fourier GR1 humanoid with two dexterous hands, standing at a kitchen counter in simulation, must pick up a wine bottle, place it into an open cabinet and then shut the cabinet. The bottle must stay inside while the door ends fully closed, so the task chains a grasp, a placement into an enclosed space and a door-closing push.

tasks.n: Move croissant from board to basket
tasks.t: A fixed-base Fourier GR1 humanoid with two dexterous hands, working at a kitchen counter in simulation, must pick a croissant off a cutting board and place it in a basket. It is a single-object transfer, so the difficulty lies in grasping a pastry with multi-finger hands and dropping it accurately into the open container.

tasks.n: Move squash from board to box
tasks.t: At a kitchen counter in simulation, a fixed-base Fourier GR1 humanoid with two dexterous hands must pick a squash up from a cutting board and put it into a cardboard box. The humanoid must grasp the vegetable with its fingers, carry it across and lower it into the box without knocking the container.

tasks.n: Move bell pepper from board to pan
tasks.t: A fixed-base Fourier GR1 humanoid with two dexterous hands, working at a kitchen counter in simulation, must pick a bell pepper off a cutting board and place it in a pan. The target is an open pan, so the humanoid must grasp the pepper with its fingers and release it over the pan.

tasks.n: Move bell pepper from board to pot
tasks.t: A fixed-base Fourier GR1 humanoid with two dexterous hands, standing at a kitchen counter in simulation, must pick a bell pepper up from a cutting board and put it into a pot. The humanoid must grasp the vegetable with its fingers and lower it past the pot's rim, so the placement needs a deliberate approach.

tasks.n: Move sweet potato to tiered basket
tasks.t: At a kitchen counter in simulation, a fixed-base Fourier GR1 humanoid with two dexterous hands must pick a sweet potato off a cutting board and place it in a tiered basket. The destination is a multi-level container, so the humanoid must grasp the vegetable with its fingers and place it in the basket without hitting the frame.

tasks.n: Move croissant from placemat to basket
tasks.t: A fixed-base Fourier GR1 humanoid with two dexterous hands, working at a kitchen counter in simulation, must pick a croissant off a placemat and place it in a basket. It is a one-object transfer, so the task mainly tests a secure grasp of a pastry with multi-finger hands and a clean release into the container.

tasks.n: Move can from placemat to bowl
tasks.t: At a kitchen counter in simulation, a fixed-base Fourier GR1 humanoid with two dexterous hands must pick a can up from a placemat and put it into a bowl. The humanoid must grasp the can securely with its fingers and set it down inside the bowl.

tasks.n: Move tomato from placemat to plate
tasks.t: A fixed-base Fourier GR1 humanoid with two dexterous hands, standing at a kitchen counter in simulation, must pick a tomato up from a placemat and place it on a plate. It is a simple one-object transfer, where the humanoid has to grasp the round fruit with its fingers and lay it down on the plate.

tasks.n: Move tomato from placemat to shelf
tasks.t: At a kitchen counter in simulation, a fixed-base Fourier GR1 humanoid with two dexterous hands must pick a tomato off a placemat and put it onto a tiered shelf. The destination has several levels, so the humanoid has to grasp the tomato with its fingers and place it on the shelf without bumping the frame.

tasks.n: Move bell pepper from plate to bowl
tasks.t: A fixed-base Fourier GR1 humanoid with two dexterous hands, working at a kitchen counter in simulation, must pick a bell pepper off a plate and place it in a bowl. The humanoid must grasp the vegetable with its fingers, lift it clear of the plate and lower it into the bowl, so the release needs to be well positioned.

tasks.n: Move lemon from plate to box
tasks.t: At a kitchen counter in simulation, a fixed-base Fourier GR1 humanoid with two dexterous hands must pick a lemon up from a plate and put it into a cardboard box. The humanoid has to grasp the fruit securely with its fingers, carry it across and lower it into the box without knocking the container.

tasks.n: Move pear from plate to pan
tasks.t: A fixed-base Fourier GR1 humanoid with two dexterous hands, standing at a kitchen counter in simulation, must pick a pear off a plate and place it in a pan. It is a one-object transfer, where the humanoid has to lift the fruit with its fingers and release it over the open pan.

tasks.n: Move sweet potato between two plates
tasks.t: At a kitchen counter in simulation, a fixed-base Fourier GR1 humanoid with two dexterous hands must lift a sweet potato from one plate and put it on another plate. Because source and target are both plates, the humanoid must tell which one holds the vegetable and move it across rather than putting it back down.

tasks.n: Move squash from tray to box
tasks.t: A fixed-base Fourier GR1 humanoid with two dexterous hands, working at a kitchen counter in simulation, must pick a squash up from a tray and put it into a cardboard box. The humanoid has to grasp the vegetable with its fingers, lift it clear of the tray and lower it into the box.

tasks.n: Move cupcake from tray to plate
tasks.t: At a kitchen counter in simulation, a fixed-base Fourier GR1 humanoid with two dexterous hands must pick a cupcake off a tray and place it on a plate. The humanoid has to grasp the cupcake with its fingers and set it down on the plate, handling the food gently.

tasks.n: Move lemon from tray to pot
tasks.t: A fixed-base Fourier GR1 humanoid with two dexterous hands, standing at a kitchen counter in simulation, must pick a lemon up from a tray and put it into a pot. The humanoid has to grasp the fruit with its fingers and lower it past the rim of the pot, so the placement needs a deliberate approach.

tasks.n: Move lemon from tray to tiered basket
tasks.t: At a kitchen counter in simulation, a fixed-base Fourier GR1 humanoid with two dexterous hands must pick a lemon off a tray and put it into a tiered basket. The destination is a multi-level container, so the humanoid has to grasp the fruit with its fingers and drop it in without hitting the frame.

tasks.n: Move bell pepper from tray to shelf
tasks.t: A fixed-base Fourier GR1 humanoid with two dexterous hands, working at a kitchen counter in simulation, must pick a bell pepper up from a tray and place it on a tiered shelf. The shelf has several levels, so the humanoid has to grasp the vegetable with its fingers and set it down on the shelf without bumping its frame.

tasks.n: Place a nut onto a peg
tasks.t: A single Sawyer arm at a table must pick up a nut and place it onto a peg, so that the nut's ring slides down around the peg. The two parts mate closely, so the grasp, the approach over the peg and the final lowering all need careful alignment before the nut is released.

tasks.n: Put a ball through a hoop
tasks.t: A single Sawyer arm at a table must pick up a ball and place it through a basketball hoop. The hoop is a small target, so the arm has to carry the ball to the right spot and let go at the right moment for it to pass through the opening, rather than just dropping it nearby.

tasks.n: Move an object between two bins
tasks.t: A single Sawyer arm at a table must pick an object up out of one bin and move it to a second, target bin. The object starts inside a container, so the gripper has to reach down past the bin's edges to grasp it, lift it clear, and carry it across to the other bin before releasing.

tasks.n: Close a box with its loose lid
tasks.t: A single Sawyer arm at a table must close a box by carrying its separate lid onto it. The lid is a free piece with a handle rather than a hinged flap, so the arm has to grasp it by the handle, lift it, bring it over the box and set it down in place.

tasks.n: Press a button straight in
tasks.t: A single Sawyer arm at a table must press a button inward. The button sits on a spring-loaded joint, so the gripper has to approach it from the right direction and push far enough against the spring for the press to count.

tasks.n: Press a button down from above
tasks.t: A single Sawyer arm at a table must press a button downward from above. The button sits on a spring-loaded joint, so the gripper has to come in over the top of it and push straight down far enough against the spring for the press to count.

tasks.n: Reach past a wall and press down
tasks.t: A single Sawyer arm at a table must reach past a wall and press a button downward. The wall gets in the way of a direct approach, so the gripper has to find a path that clears it and then push the spring-loaded button down from above.

tasks.n: Reach past a wall and press in
tasks.t: A single Sawyer arm at a table must reach past a wall and press a button inward. The wall gets in the way of a direct approach, so the gripper has to find a path that clears it and then push the spring-loaded button straight in against its spring.

tasks.n: Press the coffee machine button
tasks.t: A single Sawyer arm at a table must press the button on a coffee machine. The button sits on a spring-loaded joint on the machine, so the gripper has to locate it, line up with its direction of travel and push it in far enough for the press to register.

tasks.n: Pull a mug away from a coffee machine
tasks.t: A single Sawyer arm at a table must pull a mug away from a coffee machine until it reaches a target point. The mug starts next to the machine and has to be dragged or carried clear of it to the goal, so the grasp and the direction of motion matter, and only the mug's final position counts.

tasks.n: Push a mug under a coffee machine
tasks.t: A single Sawyer arm at a table must push a mug into a target position under a coffee machine. The mug is moved by pushing rather than lifting, so the arm has to get behind it and steer it along the table to stop at the goal beneath the machine.

tasks.n: Turn a dial to its target angle
tasks.t: A single Sawyer arm at a table must rotate a dial until a marker on its rim reaches the target position. The gripper has to make contact with the dial and turn it around its axis by the right amount, so the task rewards a controlled, contact-rich turning motion that stops at the correct angle.

tasks.n: Lift a nut off a peg
tasks.t: A single Sawyer arm at a table must lift a nut up and off the peg it sits on. This is the reverse of the nut-on-peg assembly task: the nut's ring fits around the peg, so the arm has to grasp the nut firmly and raise it cleanly clear of the peg without dragging it sideways.

tasks.n: Push a hinged door closed
tasks.t: A single Sawyer arm at a table must push a hinged door closed. The door swings about its hinge, so the gripper has to push on the panel and follow its arc until it shuts, rather than shoving it in a straight line.

tasks.n: Turn a door lock to locked
tasks.t: A single Sawyer arm at a table must move the lock of a door into its locked position. The lock is a small turning part on the door, so the gripper has to touch it precisely and rotate it the right way and by the right amount.

tasks.n: Pull a hinged door open
tasks.t: A single Sawyer arm at a table must pull a hinged door open. The door swings about its hinge, so the gripper has to take hold of it and pull along the arc of the door rather than in a straight line, keeping contact until it has swung open.

tasks.n: Turn a door lock to unlocked
tasks.t: A single Sawyer arm at a table must move the lock of a door into its unlocked position. The lock is a small turning part on the door, so the gripper has to touch it precisely and rotate it the right way and by the right amount.

tasks.n: Push a drawer closed
tasks.t: A single Sawyer arm at a table must push a drawer closed. The drawer slides along a single line, so the gripper has to contact its front and push straight along that direction until it is shut, without jamming or deflecting it sideways.

tasks.n: Pull a drawer open by its handle
tasks.t: A single Sawyer arm at a table must pull a drawer open by its handle. The drawer slides along a single direction, so the gripper has to hook or grip the handle and pull straight out along that line, keeping its hold until the drawer is open far enough.

tasks.n: Turn a faucet handle shut
tasks.t: A single Sawyer arm at a table must rotate the handle of a faucet to its closed position. The handle pivots about a joint, so the gripper has to push it around in the correct direction and through the right angle rather than just pressing on it.

tasks.n: Turn a faucet handle open
tasks.t: A single Sawyer arm at a table must rotate the handle of a faucet to its open position. The handle pivots about a joint, so the gripper has to push it around in the correct direction and through the right angle rather than just pressing on it.

tasks.n: Hammer a nail into a block
tasks.t: A single Sawyer arm at a table must grasp a hammer and use it to drive a nail well into a block. The nail only moves when the hammer strikes it squarely and firmly, so the task combines tool grasping, aiming and a hitting motion.

tasks.n: Move an object into a table opening
tasks.t: A single Sawyer arm at a table must pick up an object and move it to a target point located inside an opening in the table. The goal lies in the opening rather than on the surface, so the arm has to carry the object over the hole and lower it in before letting go.

tasks.n: Press a jointed handle downward
tasks.t: A single Sawyer arm at a table must press a handle downward. The handle is a jointed part that rotates when pushed, so the gripper has to contact it and push down far enough to swing it through its range of motion.

tasks.n: Press a handle down from the side
tasks.t: A single Sawyer arm at a table must approach a handle from the side and press it downward. The side approach means the gripper cannot simply come in from above, so it has to position itself next to the handle and push down far enough to swing the jointed handle through its range.

tasks.n: Pull a handle upward
tasks.t: A single Sawyer arm at a table must pull a handle upward. The handle is a jointed part that swings up when lifted, so the gripper has to get hold of it or hook under it and raise it far enough to move it through its range.

tasks.n: Pull a handle up from the side
tasks.t: A single Sawyer arm at a table must approach a handle from the side and pull it upward. The side approach means the gripper has to position itself next to the handle, get hold of it and raise it far enough to swing the jointed handle through its range.

tasks.n: Pull a lever through a quarter turn
tasks.t: A single Sawyer arm at a table must pull a lever to its target position, swinging it through about a quarter turn. The lever pivots on a joint, so the gripper has to hold or hook it and pull along the circular arc until the lever reaches the target.

tasks.n: Insert a peg into a side socket
tasks.t: A single Sawyer arm at a table must pick up a peg, carry it to a socket whose opening faces sideways, and insert it. The peg has to be lined up with the socket and pushed in horizontally rather than dropped from above, so alignment and contact both matter.

tasks.n: Unplug a peg from a side socket
tasks.t: A single Sawyer arm at a table must grasp a peg that sits in a side-facing socket and pull it out to a target position. The peg fits in the socket, so the arm needs a firm grasp and has to pull along the socket's axis, sideways rather than straight up, to free it cleanly.

tasks.n: Lift an object out of a hole
tasks.t: A single Sawyer arm at a table must pick an object out of a hole and lift it to a target point. The object starts down inside the hole, so the gripper has to reach into it, grasp the object and raise it clear of the edges before carrying it up to the goal.

tasks.n: Pick up and place an object
tasks.t: A single Sawyer arm at a table must pick up an object and move it to a target position. This is the basic pick-and-place skill: the arm has to reach the object, close its gripper on it, lift it, carry it to the goal and release it there.

tasks.n: Pick and place over a wall
tasks.t: A single Sawyer arm at a table must pick up an object and move it over a wall to a target position. The wall blocks a straight path, so the arm has to lift the object high enough to clear it, carry it across and then lower and release it at the goal.

tasks.n: Slide a plate forward to the target
tasks.t: A single Sawyer arm at a table must slide a plate forward into a target position. The plate is moved by pushing rather than lifting, so the arm has to contact it from behind and shove it along its path with just enough motion that it ends up at the goal.

tasks.n: Slide a plate back out to target
tasks.t: A single Sawyer arm at a table must slide a plate back out to a target position. As in the other plate-sliding tasks the plate is rearranged by pushing, not by lifting, so the arm has to get into a position that lets it move the plate backward along the table and stop at the goal.

tasks.n: Slide a plate sideways out to target
tasks.t: A single Sawyer arm at a table must slide a plate out sideways to a target position. The plate is rearranged by pushing, not by lifting, so the arm has to get alongside it and push it across the table in the sideways direction, stopping it at the goal.

tasks.n: Slide a plate sideways into target
tasks.t: A single Sawyer arm at a table must slide a plate sideways into a target position. The plate is rearranged by pushing, not by lifting, so the arm has to get alongside it and push it across the table in the sideways direction, stopping it at the goal.

tasks.n: Push an object to a target
tasks.t: A single Sawyer arm at a table must push an object across the table to a target position. The object is moved by pushing, not lifting, so the arm has to get behind it and steer it along a path that ends at the goal without knocking it past.

tasks.n: Push an object backward to target
tasks.t: A single Sawyer arm at a table must push an object backward to a target position. The object is moved by pushing, not lifting, so the arm has to get into a position that lets it shove the object back along the table and stop it at the goal.

tasks.n: Push an object around a wall
tasks.t: A single Sawyer arm at a table must push an object around a wall to a target position. The wall blocks the direct line to the goal, so the arm has to steer the object along a curved path past the wall, without lifting it, and leave it at the target.

tasks.n: Reach a target position
tasks.t: A single Sawyer arm at a table must move its gripper to a given target position. Nothing has to be grasped or moved, so this is a pure reaching task that checks whether the agent can drive the arm accurately from its start pose to a point in space.

tasks.n: Reach a target around a wall
tasks.t: A single Sawyer arm at a table must move its gripper around a wall to a target position. Nothing has to be grasped; the difficulty is that the wall blocks the direct route, so the arm must choose a path that goes around it and still ends precisely at the target.

tasks.n: Place an object on a shelf
tasks.t: A single Sawyer arm at a table must pick up an object and place it on a shelf at the target position. The goal is on the shelf rather than on the table, so the arm has to lift the object to the right height, move it in over the shelf and set it down there.

tasks.n: Push a soccer ball into a goal
tasks.t: A single Sawyer arm at a table must push a soccer ball into a goal. The ball rolls when pushed, so the arm has to hit it in the right direction with a suitable amount of motion, without letting it veer off or roll past the goal.

tasks.n: Hook a thermos with a stick and pull
tasks.t: A single Sawyer arm at a table must grasp a stick, hook it into the handle of a thermos, and use it to pull the thermos to a target point, with the stick still in the handle at the end. The thermos is moved only through the tool, so aligning the stick with the handle and keeping it hooked while pulling are the hard parts.

tasks.n: Push a thermos with a stick
tasks.t: A single Sawyer arm at a table must grasp a stick and use it to push a thermos to a target point, while still holding the stick lifted at the end. The thermos is moved only through the tool, so the arm has to control the stick's tip and push along the right direction.

tasks.n: Sweep an object to a target spot
tasks.t: A single Sawyer arm at a table must sweep a small object across the surface until it comes to rest at a marked target position. Rather than grasping it, the arm pushes the object along with its gripper, so success depends on how contact moves a free-sliding object, and the object and goal positions come from one fixed random layout.

tasks.n: Sweep an object into an opening
tasks.t: A single Sawyer arm at a table must sweep a small object across the surface and into an opening. The arm pushes the object with its gripper instead of picking it up, so it has to steer a free-sliding object along a path that ends exactly in the opening, starting from one fixed random layout of object and goal.

tasks.n: Slide a window closed
tasks.t: A single Sawyer arm at a table must push a small sliding window shut. The window moves along just one direction of travel, so the arm has to place the gripper against the sash and push along that line, and the exact window placement comes from one fixed random layout.

tasks.n: Slide a window open
tasks.t: A single Sawyer arm at a table must push a small sliding window open. The window moves along just one direction of travel, so the arm has to engage the sash with its gripper and drag it along that line, and the exact window placement comes from one fixed random layout.

tasks.n: Pocket the ball worth seven points
tasks.t: A Franka Panda arm is asked to put the ball worth seven points into the middle pocket on its right side of the table. The request refers to a ball by its game value, which is the black ball in snooker, so the arm needs common-sense knowledge of the game and colour recognition to choose the ball before pocketing it.

tasks.n: Take out the permanganate tube
tasks.t: A Franka Panda arm must take the tube holding potassium permanganate solution out of a rack, choosing among tubes with iron chloride and iodine and no name tags. The right tube has to be found from its colour combined with basic chemistry knowledge, and then pulled out of the stand.

tasks.n: Put the pear on the plate
tasks.t: A Franka Panda arm must put a pear on a plate, choosing it from four fruits on the table: pear, peach, mango and orange. Several of them look alike at first glance, so the arm has to use its knowledge of what a pear looks like before carrying the right fruit to the plate.

tasks.n: Tip a sauce bottle over a pan
tasks.t: A Franka Panda arm must add barbecue sauce to a dish by holding the sauce bottle over a pan and tipping it past horizontal, though no liquid is actually simulated. The arm has to pick the right bottle from among salt and salad dressing and then perform a pouring-like tilt over the pan.

tasks.n: Shelve three books by publication date
tasks.t: A Franka Panda arm must move three books from the table into a bookshelf, side by side, so that they run from oldest to newest from left to right as seen from the robot. The books are identified by title and the order depends on knowing when each was published, so the task mixes reading, common-sense knowledge and an ordering puzzle with careful shelf placement.

tasks.n: Find an apple in a cabinet
tasks.t: A Franka Panda arm is asked to find the apple and take it out of a cabinet. The apple is not in view at the start but sits in one of the cabinet's drawers, so the arm must search by opening the drawer, then pick the apple out and bring it clear of the cabinet.

tasks.n: Hammer a nail and hang a painting
tasks.t: A Franka Panda arm must hang a named painting on the wall securely by first driving a nail into the wall with a hammer and then bringing the painting to the nail. The arm has to pick the right painting by its title from among others, use the hammer as a tool to seat the nail, and finish with an accurate hand-off of the picture onto the nail.

tasks.n: Heat food in a microwave
tasks.t: A Franka Panda arm must heat the cooked food from a tray of three items by putting it into the microwave, closing the door and pressing the start button, though the heating itself is not simulated. The cooked dish must be picked out from the ingredients by sight, and the steps depend on each other, ending with the door shut and the start button pressed.

tasks.n: Put the blooming tulip in a vase
tasks.t: A Franka Panda arm must insert a tulip into a vase. Among the flowers on the table, the blooming tulip has to be chosen over two wilted flowers, and the vase opening is narrow, so the arm needs both a correct visual choice and a careful, contact-aware insertion of the stem.

tasks.n: Put a rose in a vase
tasks.t: A Franka Panda arm must insert a rose into a vase. The rose has to be chosen from among other flowers on the table, a chrysanthemum and a sunflower, and the vase opening is narrow, so the arm needs both a correct visual choice and a careful, contact-aware insertion of the stem.

tasks.n: Spell a word problem's answer with cubes
tasks.t: A Franka Panda arm is given a short word problem about a mechanic's repair revenue and must answer it by laying number cubes side by side on a placemat so that they spell the correct figure from left to right. It has to read the digit cubes, solve the arithmetic, and place the right cubes in the right order, so reasoning and arrangement are both needed.

tasks.n: Put a box on a named painting
tasks.t: A Franka Panda arm must set a box down on top of one particular painting, Dinner and Love on the River, among several paintings. The arm has to recognise the named artwork and tell it apart from the others using art knowledge before carrying the box to it and placing it there.

tasks.n: Put striped ball in middle pocket
tasks.t: A Franka Panda arm must find the striped ball numbered fourteen among five billiard balls and put it into the middle pocket on its right side of the table. The ball has to be recognised by its number and stripe, and then carried and dropped accurately into one particular pocket.

tasks.n: Take out the copper chloride tube
tasks.t: A Franka Panda arm must take a test tube holding copper chloride solution out of a rack. Another tube holds copper sulfate, and the two are told apart by their name tags or colour, so the arm must recognise the right tube before pulling it out of the stand.

tasks.n: Take juice out of the fridge
tasks.t: A Franka Panda arm must take a juice drink out of an open fridge. The fridge also holds another drink, so the arm has to identify the juice by sight before reaching in to grasp it and bring it out of the fridge.

tasks.n: Put the banana on the plate
tasks.t: A Franka Panda arm must pick the banana from among an orange and a mango on the table and put it on a plate. The fruits have to be told apart by sight, so the main difficulty is choosing the right one before an ordinary pick and place.

tasks.n: Put a named mahjong tile on a mat
tasks.t: A Franka Panda arm must find the mahjong tile showing six of the bamboo suit among seven tiles and put it on a placemat. The tiles differ only by the symbols on their faces, so the arm has to read them correctly before picking up the right small tile.

tasks.n: Pick up the smallest playing card
tasks.t: A Franka Panda arm must pick up the smallest of four playing cards from a card holder and hold it up in the air. The arm has to read and compare the ranks of the cards to find the smallest, and then grasp a thin card out of its holder and lift it clear.

tasks.n: Pick the ukiyo-e painting
tasks.t: A Franka Panda arm must select the painting in the ukiyo-e style by pressing the button in front of it. The other paintings are in realist and minimalist styles, so the arm has to recognise the art style by sight before making a precise button press.

tasks.n: Pick up the ace of hearts
tasks.t: A Franka Panda arm must pick up the ace of hearts from four playing cards standing in a holder and hold it up in the air. The card has to be recognised by sight among the others, and then a thin card must be grasped out of the holder and lifted clear.

tasks.n: Take the history book off the shelf
tasks.t: A single Franka arm faces a bookshelf and must pull out the one book about history and take it off the shelf. The books are told apart only by their subject titles, with decoys on topics such as electronics, data visualisation and quantum dots, so the arm has to read and categorise the titles before choosing which book to grasp.

tasks.n: Put the Mickey toy in the gift box
tasks.t: A single Franka arm at a table must pick the Mickey figure out of a small group of cartoon and superhero toys and put it into a gift box. Several look-alike character toys act as decoys, so the arm has to recognise the right character by appearance before it grasps, carries and drops the toy into the box.

tasks.n: Place the odd mahjong tile on the mat
tasks.t: A single Franka arm facing a scattering of mahjong tiles must find the one tile that belongs to a different suit from all the others and put it on a placemat. The task is an odd-one-out judgement over tile faces, so the arm has to recognise the suits visually and ignore the many look-alike tiles before it grasps the right one.

tasks.n: Fetch a healthy drink from the fridge
tasks.t: A single Franka arm is told that the user is thirsty after sport and wants something healthy and cool, so it must open a small fridge, take the suitable drink out and close the door again. The drinks are hidden until the door is open and the right one must be chosen by common sense from several beverages, making this a short ordered sequence of open, fetch and close.

tasks.n: Show a poker hand on the placemat
tasks.t: A single Franka arm is invited to a game of Texas hold'em and must show a straight running from six to ten, picking the five named playing cards out of a larger set standing in holders and laying them on a placemat. The cards are told apart only by reading their faces, so the arm must identify each requested card among similar ones and place all five.

tasks.n: Pick the slowest-sliding object
tasks.t: A Franka Panda arm faces a small science question: which of the objects on display would slide the slowest down a steel ramp. It answers by pressing the button in front of the chosen object, so the hard part is common-sense physics from appearance, telling sliding from rolling among two cylinders and a box, before a precise button press.

tasks.n: Choose the magnetic object
tasks.t: A Franka Panda arm is told about an experiment on which objects are magnetic and must choose the magnetic one by pressing the button in front of it. The candidates are made of different materials, stone, metal and wood, so the arm must recognise materials by sight and apply simple science knowledge before a precise button press.
st: objects of stone, metal and wood

tasks.n: Pick the most reflective mirror
tasks.t: A Franka Panda arm must choose the mirror with the largest reflection and signal its choice by pressing the button in front of it. The mirrors differ only in how reflective they look when rendered, so the choice rests purely on visual perception, followed by a precise press of the correct button.

tasks.n: Fetch a named tube from conversation
tasks.t: A Franka Panda arm is asked, in conversational wording, to take out the potassium permanganate solution from a rack of test tubes. The three tubes carry name tags, so the arm must read the tags to identify the right one and then pull it out of the stand.

tasks.n: Play a mahjong tile from conversation
tasks.t: A Franka Panda arm is asked in conversational wording, as if replacing a mahjong player, to take out the nine of the characters suit and put that tile on a placemat. The tile must be found among seven by reading its face, so the arm has to interpret the request and then pick the right tile.

tasks.n: Pick up the six of spades
tasks.t: A Franka Panda arm must pick up the six of spades from four playing cards standing in a holder and hold it up in the air. The card has to be recognised by its rank and suit among the others, and then a thin card must be grasped out of the holder and lifted clear.

tasks.n: Put striped ball in corner pocket
tasks.t: A Franka Panda arm must find the striped ball numbered fourteen among five billiard balls and put it into the right-bottom corner pocket of the table. The ball has to be recognised by its number and stripe, and the pocket is named by its position, so the arm must also work out which of the pockets is meant.

tasks.n: Take the second book from the left
tasks.t: A Franka Panda arm must take the second book from the left, as seen from the robot, on the top layer out of a bookshelf. The book is specified only by its ordinal position, so the arm has to work out which one is meant and then pull it cleanly out of the shelf.

tasks.n: Take the tube by grid position
tasks.t: A Franka Panda arm must take out the test tube in the first row and fifth column of a rack of tubes. The tube is given only by its position in the grid, so the arm has to work out which one is meant and then pull it out of the stand without disturbing its neighbours.

tasks.n: Take the seventh mahjong tile
tasks.t: A Franka Panda arm must put the seventh mahjong tile from the left, as seen from the robot, on a placemat. The tile is specified only by its position in the row of tiles, so the arm has to count along the row to work out which one is meant before picking it up.

tasks.n: Pick up the fourth card from left
tasks.t: A Franka Panda arm must pick up the fourth playing card from the left, as seen from the robot, out of its holder and hold it up in the air. The card is specified only by its position in the row, so the arm has to count along the cards before grasping the thin card and lifting it clear.

tasks.n: Balance on a rolling board
tasks.t: A Unitree H1 humanoid starts standing on a balance board that rides on top of a rolling sphere and must stay on it, upright and still, for the whole episode. The footing is inherently unstable, so the humanoid needs constant fine balance corrections with gentle joint effort, and the episode is lost as soon as the board touches the ground or the humanoid sags too low.

tasks.n: Run a hurdle track
tasks.t: A Unitree H1 humanoid must run forward down a walled track past a line of hurdles without touching the side or back walls and without falling. The target pace is a sprint rather than a walk, and each hurdle is a solid barrier across the whole track that has to be cleared, so slow, quasi-static motion cannot succeed.

tasks.n: Sit down on a chair
tasks.t: A Unitree H1 humanoid must lower itself onto a chair and stay seated, upright and still. The challenge is the transition: it has to bring its pelvis over the seat and settle to seated height quickly yet steadily, without toppling or ending up beside the chair, and then hold the seated posture with little effort.

tasks.n: Walk forward without falling
tasks.t: A Unitree H1 humanoid on flat ground must walk forward at a modest walking pace and keep walking without falling over. It is the basic locomotion test: the gait has to make steady forward progress, stay upright and use little actuator effort, because any fall ends the episode.

tasks.n: Shelve five objects in shade order
tasks.t: A Unitree H1 humanoid with two five-finger Shadow hands must pick five red-tinted objects out of a set of twelve, the other seven being grey, and put each on its own place on a bookshelf, one at a time, from palest to darkest. Each destination is shown only as a translucent copy of the object, so the robot has to rank objects by shade and carry out five placements in the required order.

tasks.n: Rotate cubes in both hands
tasks.t: A Unitree H1 humanoid with two Shadow hands has a cube starting just above each palm and must rotate both cubes to a goal orientation without dropping either one. The target is shown only as a translucent cube, and close is not good enough because only a precise orientation match counts, so both hands need careful in-hand finger work while the humanoid keeps standing still.

tasks.n: Walk through a heavy door
tasks.t: A Unitree H1 humanoid must walk up to a closed door, press its handle, pull the hinged door open towards itself and then walk through to the other side. It combines walking with a contact-heavy interaction with an articulated object: the door is heavy, so the humanoid has to open it while staying upright and then carry its torso through the doorway.

tasks.n: Lift a dumbbell overhead
tasks.t: A Unitree H1 humanoid with two Shadow hands must lift a very heavy dumbbell from the floor to well above its head and keep it there for most of the episode. This is a whole-body effort with no balance controller supplied: the humanoid has to grip the weight, drive it upward using its whole body, and stay standing while holding it aloft.

tasks.n: Gather scattered room objects
tasks.t: A Unitree H1 humanoid with two Shadow hands must tidy a room by gathering six loose objects (a chair, a trophy, headphones, two packages and a snow globe) close together instead of spread out. No target positions are given and the objects start out of reach, so the humanoid has to walk around, find the right items among fixed furniture such as a table and bookshelf, and move them one by one.

tasks.n: Wipe a window with a tool
tasks.t: A Unitree H1 humanoid with two Shadow hands must catch a wiping tool that starts in mid-air in front of its hands and falls almost at once unless gripped, then use it to wipe a window with steady up-and-down strokes. The tool has to stay pressed against the glass, so the task needs a quick grasp followed by sustained contact while both hands keep hold.

tasks.n: Close a cabinet door in a house
tasks.t: A Franka arm with a two-finger Robotiq gripper on a fixed base, set in a simulated house, must shut a cabinet whose hinged door starts about half open. The door must end up nearly closed and stay that way, so the arm has to push a swinging door through its arc and not leave it drifting back open.

tasks.n: Open a dishwasher in a house
tasks.t: A Franka arm with a two-finger Robotiq gripper on a fixed base, set in a simulated house, must pull a dishwasher door away from its closed position by a clear amount. Any dishwasher in the room counts, so the arm first has to find one and then work out where to grip or hook the hinged door to swing it open.

tasks.n: Pick up a pie in a house
tasks.t: A Franka arm with a two-finger Robotiq gripper on a fixed base, set in a simulated house, must pick up a pie and lift it a little clear of where it sat. At the end only the robot may be touching the pie, and since it is an irregular model from a large library of 3D assets, a suitable grasp has to be found from the scene.

tasks.n: Put a bottle into an ashtray
tasks.t: A Franka arm with a two-finger Robotiq gripper on a fixed base, set in a simulated house, must pick up a purple bottle with a white cap and set it in or on a clear ashtray with notches. Both objects are named only by appearance, and the gripper must let go cleanly so the ashtray holds the bottle without being knocked far out of place.

tasks.n: Place an object in the right-colour bowl
tasks.t: A Franka arm with a two-finger Robotiq gripper on a fixed base, set in a simulated house, must pick up a small dark bird and put it in or on the red bowl. A second receptacle of a different colour is also present and does not count, so the arm must tell the two apart by colour before placing the bird and releasing it.

tasks.n: Place an object next to bread
tasks.t: A Franka arm with a two-finger Robotiq gripper on a fixed base, set in a simulated house, must pick up a compact black rail mount with slots and set it down close beside a loaf of bread, on the same surface. The bread must stay put, and both items are known only from descriptions, so this is about placing relative to another object rather than at a fixed spot.

tasks.n: Find and approach a table lamp
tasks.t: A Rainbow RB-Y1 wheeled mobile manipulator with two arms and a head camera starts in an unfamiliar house and must drive up to a table lamp until it is close and the lamp is visible in its camera. Two lamps exist and the nearest counts, but the nearest is out of view at the start, so the robot must explore across rooms and recognise the lamp from its category alone.

tasks.n: Pull a door open with RB-Y1
tasks.t: A Rainbow RB-Y1 wheeled mobile manipulator, with a torso, two arms and a head camera, must pull a door open in a simulated house until the door has swung most of the way open. The door turns on a hinge and has to be pulled, not pushed, so the robot must combine base, torso and arm motion to sweep it through its arc.

tasks.n: Rods into narrow cupboards
tasks.t: A TidyBot++ wheeled mobile manipulator with a seven-joint arm and a two-finger gripper must pick six brown rods off the floor and put each one into its own tall compartment in a row of narrow cupboards. The rods look identical, so the pairing has to be worked out from their ranking and the cupboard order, and the tight fit of each rod in its slot demands precise placement.

tasks.n: Drive into the green square
tasks.t: A TidyBot++ wheeled mobile manipulator must drive its base into a translucent green square marked on the floor while three chairs stand in the way. The chairs can be pushed aside, and red, blue and yellow squares nearby only show where the chairs started, so the robot has to pick out the true goal square and plan a path that shoves the furniture clear.

tasks.n: Sweep cubes into a drawer
tasks.t: A TidyBot++ wheeled mobile manipulator must get five small cubes from the top of a kitchen island into the middle drawer of its upper row, using a wiper that lies beside them. The drawer starts closed, so the robot must first pull it open, then sweep the cubes off the island edge into it with sustained wiper contact, leaving every cube comfortably inside.

tasks.n: Scoop cubes between bins
tasks.t: A TidyBot++ wheeled mobile manipulator with an arm and gripper must move a large number of small dark-red cubes from a yellow bin into a green bin, with a scoop available in the scene. Carrying cubes one at a time would be far too slow, so the task favours using the scoop to transfer many per trip and tip them in, leaving every cube settled inside, clear of the rim and walls.

tasks.n: Sweep floor cubes into a box
tasks.t: A TidyBot++ wheeled mobile manipulator must gather many small dark-red cubes scattered on the floor into a translucent grey box marked at the end of a kitchen island nearest to it, using a wiper that stands close by. Pushing so many loose cubes into a small target calls for a sweeping plan with repeated base and arm motions, since picking them up individually would be far too slow.

tasks.n: Copy Cézanne's Apples and Oranges in acrylic
tasks.t: A single Franka arm holding a round acrylic brush must reproduce a small acrylic painting after Paul Cézanne's Still Life with Apples and Oranges from a reference image onto a square sheet, loading the brush from a palette of premixed paint wells within a stroke cap. Colours must be matched to the wells and placed from the image, mark width depends on press depth and must be learned from test strokes, and later strokes cover earlier ones.
st: acrylic copy of Cezanne still life with apples and oranges
