tasks.n: Lift a bottle head-up
tasks.t: A dual-arm ALOHA-AgileX robot at a table must pick up a bottle lying on its side and lift it clear of the table with the head pointing up. The robot has to choose the arm on the bottle's side of the table and turn the bottle upright as it lifts, so the task mixes arm selection with a re-orienting grasp.

tasks.n: Hit a block with a hammer
tasks.t: A dual-arm ALOHA-AgileX robot at a table must pick up a hammer and strike a block with it, bringing the hammer head down onto the block. Besides grasping a tool by its handle, the robot must carry it through a swing and land the head right on the target, which needs accurate placement and contact.

tasks.n: Rank blocks by color
tasks.t: A dual-arm ALOHA-AgileX robot at a table must line up a red, a green and a blue block in a row, in that order from left to right. The robot has to read the order from color, move three blocks to the right slots with whichever arm suits each, and finish with both grippers open and the row neat.

tasks.n: Rank blocks by size
tasks.t: A dual-arm ALOHA-AgileX robot at a table must move three blocks of random colors to the middle of the table and line them up in a row from the largest to the smallest, left to right. The order depends on how big each block looks rather than on its color, so the robot must judge sizes by sight, plan the placements and finish with both grippers open.

tasks.n: Dump balls into the big bin
tasks.t: A dual-arm ALOHA-AgileX robot must grab a small bin on a table and tip its balls into a big bin standing on the floor, finishing with the small bin held up. The robot has to lift and tilt the bin at the right moment so every ball lands in the big bin, which makes this a pouring task with loose, rolling contents.

tasks.n: Grab a roller with both arms
tasks.t: A dual-arm ALOHA-AgileX robot at a table must take hold of a roller with both grippers at once and lift it off the table. Because the roller is held at both ends, the two arms have to reach their grasp points together and close at the same time, so the task is mostly about coordination between the arms.

tasks.n: Hand a block over and place it
tasks.t: A dual-arm ALOHA-AgileX robot at a table must pick up a red block with its left arm, pass it to its right arm in mid-air, and have the right arm set it down on a blue pad. The hard part is the exchange: the second hand must take over the block cleanly before it is placed on the pad, so the task needs timing and coordination between the arms.

tasks.n: Hand a microphone to the other arm
tasks.t: A dual-arm ALOHA-AgileX robot at a table must pick up a microphone with one arm and pass it to the other arm, which then holds it up. The arm that grabs first depends on where the microphone lies, and the pass has to leave it held by the second arm only, so the task tests a clean handover and a regrasp.

tasks.n: Hang a mug on a rack
tasks.t: A dual-arm ALOHA-AgileX robot at a table must pick up a mug with its left arm, turn it and set it down in the middle, then take it with its right arm and hang it by the handle on a rack. It is a long two-stage task that includes a regrasp between the arms and a precise hanging motion, since the handle has to land on the rack arm.

tasks.n: Lift a pot with both arms
tasks.t: A dual-arm ALOHA-AgileX robot at a table must lift a pot using both arms, each taking one of its handles. The arms have to grip the handles together and raise the pot without tilting it, so the task is about synchronized contact and a stable shared load.

tasks.n: Move a can beside a pot
tasks.t: A dual-arm ALOHA-AgileX robot at a table must pick up a can with one arm and set it down upright next to a pot. The robot has to pick the arm that suits where the can lies and put the can on the right side of the pot without tipping it, which is a simple but position-sensitive placement.

tasks.n: Move a pill bottle onto a pad
tasks.t: A dual-arm ALOHA-AgileX robot at a table must pick up a pill bottle with one arm and place it on a pad. The small bottle must be grasped and set down accurately on the pad with the gripper let go, so the task tests a careful pick-and-place with the right choice of arm.

tasks.n: Move a playing card outward
tasks.t: A dual-arm ALOHA-AgileX robot at a table must pick up a playing card and move it outward, away from the middle of the table, on whichever side it already lies. A thin card lying flat is awkward to grasp, and the robot has to read which way is outward for the card before choosing the arm and the carry direction.

tasks.n: Move a stapler onto a mat
tasks.t: A dual-arm ALOHA-AgileX robot at a table must pick the suitable arm and use it to move a stapler onto a colored mat, leaving it flat and lined up with the mat. The stapler has to land centered and with the right orientation, so the task combines choosing an arm with a fairly exact placement.

tasks.n: Open a laptop
tasks.t: A dual-arm ALOHA-AgileX robot at a table must open a closed laptop with one arm, swinging the lid up about its hinge to a clear opening. The lid is an articulated part, so the robot has to find a good place to push or lift it and follow the hinge's arc without shoving the laptop away.

tasks.n: Open a microwave door
tasks.t: A dual-arm ALOHA-AgileX robot must open the door of a microwave by pulling it round its hinge until it is well open. The door is an articulated part that swings through an arc, so the robot has to hook or grip the door and follow its path rather than push straight back.

tasks.n: Pick two varied bottles, one per arm
tasks.t: A dual-arm ALOHA-AgileX robot at a table must pick up one bottle with one arm and a second bottle with the other arm at the same time, and hold both up in front of it. The bottles come from a varied set, so each grasp has to suit its bottle, and the two arms must work side by side without getting in each other's way.

tasks.n: Pick two bottles with both arms
tasks.t: A dual-arm ALOHA-AgileX robot at a table must pick up one bottle with one arm and a second bottle with the other arm at the same time, and hold both up in front of it. Each arm has to reach its own bottle and lift it to its own hold position, so the task tests parallel grasping and keeping the two arms from colliding.

tasks.n: Place one object left of another
tasks.t: A dual-arm ALOHA-AgileX robot at a table must pick up one object with a suitable arm and set it down on the left side of a second object, close beside it. Only the first object moves, and the result is judged by where it sits relative to the other, so the task tests the robot's sense of left and right and a controlled placement.

tasks.n: Place one object right of another
tasks.t: A dual-arm ALOHA-AgileX robot at a table must pick up one object and set it down to the right of a second, stationary object, using whichever arm suits the layout. The object has to end up a modest distance to the right and roughly level with the other one, with both grippers released, so the task is about relative position rather than a fixed spot.

tasks.n: Put bread into a basket
tasks.t: A dual-arm ALOHA-AgileX robot at a table must put every piece of bread lying there into a basket. The scene holds either one or two breads: with one, a single arm carries it over, and with two, both arms grab them at the same time, so the robot has to read the layout and choose between single-arm and coordinated dual-arm picking.

tasks.n: Put bread into a skillet
tasks.t: A dual-arm ALOHA-AgileX robot picks a piece of bread off the table and puts it into a skillet, and at the end the skillet must be held up off the table with the bread inside. The final state involves two objects at once, the bread in the pan and the pan raised, so the robot cannot simply drop the bread in and leave the pan resting.

tasks.n: Put burger and fries on a tray
tasks.t: A dual-arm ALOHA-AgileX robot picks up a toy hamburger and a portion of french fries and places them on a tray, each onto its own marked spot. Both arms are meant to be used, and the robot has to recognise which item belongs where and set each one down accurately enough to land on its own spot.

tasks.n: Put can in basket, then lift basket
tasks.t: A dual-arm ALOHA-AgileX robot puts a can into a basket and then lifts the basket with its other arm, holding it up and upright with the can still inside. The two arms play different roles in sequence, and the basket must be raised clear of the table and kept level so that the can stays in the basket rather than touching the table.

tasks.n: Place two cans in a plastic box
tasks.t: A dual-arm ALOHA-AgileX robot picks up two cans and places them into a plastic box, each onto one of the box's two designated spots. Using both arms lets the cans go in together, and the placements must be accurate enough that each can ends at its own spot rather than anywhere inside the box.

tasks.n: Place a container on a plate
tasks.t: A dual-arm ALOHA-AgileX robot picks up a container from the table and sets it down on a plate, then releases it. The container must come to rest on the plate close to its centre with both grippers open, so the main challenge is a clean, well-aligned placement of the container, whichever shape it happens to have.

tasks.n: Put a pair of shoes in a box
tasks.t: A dual-arm ALOHA-AgileX robot uses both arms to pick up the two shoes lying on the table and put them into a shoebox, each at its own spot with the toe pointing left. The shoes must end up in the right position and heading, so each grasp has to allow the shoe to be turned and set down correctly.

tasks.n: Place an empty cup on a coaster
tasks.t: A dual-arm ALOHA-AgileX robot uses one arm to pick up an empty cup from the table and set it down on a coaster, then let go. The cup has to sit centred on the coaster at the right height, so the task is mostly about picking the cup in a way that allows an accurate and stable placement.

tasks.n: Place a fan on a mat facing the robot
tasks.t: A dual-arm ALOHA-AgileX robot grabs a fan and places it on a coloured mat so that the fan ends up facing the robot. Both the position on the mat and the fan's orientation matter, so the robot has to choose a grasp that lets it turn the fan the right way while setting it down.

tasks.n: Place a mouse on a coloured mat
tasks.t: A dual-arm ALOHA-AgileX robot grabs a computer mouse and places it on a coloured mat, with the mouse lying along the mat's long side. Both the position on the mat and the mouse's alignment must be right, and the robot must release it afterwards, so accurate placement matters more than the pick itself.

tasks.n: Put object in basket, move basket
tasks.t: A dual-arm ALOHA-AgileX robot uses one arm to put a target object into a basket, then grabs the basket with the other arm and moves it slightly away, lifting it with the object inside. The arms work in sequence on two items, and the basket has to stay upright and carry the object rather than leave it resting on the table.

tasks.n: Place an object on a scale
tasks.t: A dual-arm ALOHA-AgileX robot picks one object off the table with a single arm and sets it onto a scale, then releases it. The object has to end up on the scale's weighing surface, so the main demands are recognising the object and the scale and placing the object accurately and steadily.

tasks.n: Place an object on a display stand
tasks.t: A dual-arm ALOHA-AgileX robot picks up an object with whichever arm is suitable and places it on a display stand, then releases it. The object must come to rest over the stand, so the robot has to pick a grasp suited to the object's shape and set it down steadily on a fairly restricted support.

tasks.n: Put a phone on a stand
tasks.t: A dual-arm ALOHA-AgileX robot picks up a phone from the table and puts it on a phone stand. The phone must end up seated on the stand in the right position and alignment, so the robot needs a grasp that lets it set the phone down accurately rather than just dropping it near the stand.

tasks.n: Place a shoe on a mat, tip left
tasks.t: A dual-arm ALOHA-AgileX robot uses one arm to take a shoe from the table and place it on a mat, with the toe pointing to the left. Besides reaching the mat, the shoe has to be turned to the required heading, so the grasp must allow both the transport and the reorientation.

tasks.n: Press down a stapler
tasks.t: A dual-arm ALOHA-AgileX robot uses one arm to press down the hinged top of a stapler standing on the table. The gripper has to touch the stapler at its press point and push the top half down, so the task is about locating the right spot and applying a downward push through contact.

tasks.n: Put three bottles in a dustbin
tasks.t: A dual-arm ALOHA-AgileX robot must get all three bottles from the table into a dustbin standing on the floor at its left. Only the left arm can reach the bin, so bottles on the right half of the table have to be handed over in mid-air from the right arm to the left, making a long sequence of picks, handovers and drops.
st: bottles from the right half of the table

tasks.n: Rotate a QR board to face robot
tasks.t: A dual-arm ALOHA-AgileX robot picks up a QR-code board from the table, turns it, and sets it back upright so that the code faces the robot. The board has to end in one specific orientation, so the robot must plan a grasp that allows the rotation and then put the board down steadily.

tasks.n: Scan a held tea box
tasks.t: A dual-arm ALOHA-AgileX robot picks up a scanner with one arm and a tea box with the other, lifts the box in front of itself and points the scanner's head at it from just a short distance so it can be scanned. Both items stay in the grippers at the end, so the arms must hold a steady, accurate pose relative to each other.

tasks.n: Pick up and shake a bottle
tasks.t: A dual-arm ALOHA-AgileX robot picks up a bottle with a suitable arm and shakes it. The outcome is judged by whether the bottle ends up held clear of the table, so what matters most is choosing the right arm and keeping a secure grasp while the bottle is moved back and forth.

tasks.n: Shake a bottle horizontally
tasks.t: A dual-arm ALOHA-AgileX robot picks up a bottle with a suitable arm and shakes it sideways rather than up and down. The outcome is judged by whether the bottle ends up held clear of the table, so the robot needs the right arm and a secure grasp that survives the horizontal swinging motion.

tasks.n: Stack three coloured blocks
tasks.t: A dual-arm ALOHA-AgileX robot gathers a red, a green and a blue block at the centre of the table and stacks them with blue on top of green and green on top of red. The order is given by colour, so the robot must tell the blocks apart and build the tower from the bottom up, keeping each level steady.

tasks.n: Stack green block on red block
tasks.t: A dual-arm ALOHA-AgileX robot picks up a green cube and stacks it on top of a red cube with either arm, then opens its grippers so the stack stays put. The two cubes look alike apart from colour, so the robot must use colour to decide which goes on top and place it squarely so that it rests on the lower one.

tasks.n: Stack three bowls
tasks.t: A dual-arm ALOHA-AgileX robot stacks three bowls from the table into a single pile. Each round bowl has to be set squarely onto the one below, and the pile becomes less forgiving with every bowl added, so the robot must place carefully and keep the whole stack from toppling.

tasks.n: Stack two bowls
tasks.t: A dual-arm ALOHA-AgileX robot picks up one bowl from the table and stacks it on top of another so the two form a single pile. The upper bowl has to sit squarely on the lower one, so the task rewards a grasp that gives a clean, centred release over the other bowl.

tasks.n: Stamp a seal on a coloured mat
tasks.t: A dual-arm ALOHA-AgileX robot grabs a stamp and presses it down onto a mat of a specified colour, then lets go. The stamp has to land accurately at the centre of the right mat, so the robot must pick out the correct colour and set the stamp down precisely as a tool rather than just placing an object.

tasks.n: Flip a switch with the arm
tasks.t: A dual-arm ALOHA-AgileX robot uses an arm to click a switch, flipping its lever to the far end of its travel. The switch is a small hinged mechanism, so the task is about locating it and giving a clean push in the right direction until the lever reaches its limit.

tasks.n: Hand a box between ALOHA arms
tasks.t: An ALOHA 2 bimanual robot, with two arms facing each other across a table, must pick up a red box with its left arm, pass it to the right arm, and have the right arm hold it at a floating target box. The exchange needs both grippers to coordinate in mid-air, and the box must then be held steady at the target position.

tasks.n: Insert a peg into a socket with two arms
tasks.t: An ALOHA 2 bimanual robot must pick up a blue square-tube socket with one arm and a red peg with the other, lift both, and push the end of the peg into the open end of the socket. Neither part is fixed to the table, so the two arms must align and mate two free-floating objects with tight clearance.

tasks.n: Pull a cabinet handle to a target
tasks.t: A Franka Panda arm faces a green handle mounted on a short slide in front of a shelf and must grasp the handle and pull it along its slide to a marked red target. The handle moves along only one line, so the arm needs a firm grip and a straight pull that stops where the target is.

tasks.n: Pick a box and match target orientation
tasks.t: A Franka Panda arm must pick up a small green box from the floor and hold it at a translucent red target box floating above, matching both the target position and its tilted orientation. The grasp therefore has to rotate the box into a specific pose in the air, and not only lift it to the right place.

tasks.n: Barkour tracks joystick commands under pushes
tasks.t: A Google Barkour quadruped standing on flat ground must follow a schedule of velocity commands covering forward, sideways and turning motion for a whole episode without falling. The torso is also shoved several times in random directions, so the legged robot has to keep walking and recover its balance after each push while still matching the commanded motion.

tasks.n: Go1 balances on its hind legs
tasks.t: A Unitree Go1 quadruped starting from its normal stance must rear up onto its hind legs with its nose pointing upward and both front feet off the ground, then hold that pose for a couple of seconds. It must not topple or let any other leg part touch the floor, so the balance has to be stable and not a brief lunge.

tasks.n: Go1 gets up after a fall
tasks.t: A Unitree Go1 quadruped lies tipped over on flat ground after a drop, in an awkward pose with randomly bent legs. It must roll or push itself back onto its feet and stand upright at its normal height, holding that stance briefly, which needs a sequence of ground contacts and shifts of weight from a poorly posed start.

tasks.n: Go1 handstand on its front legs
tasks.t: A Unitree Go1 quadruped starting from its normal stance must tip forward into a handstand, balancing on its front legs with its nose down and both hind feet in the air, and hold it for a couple of seconds. The pose is inherently unstable and no other leg part may touch the floor, so the balance has to be actively maintained.

tasks.n: Go1 follows joystick commands on flat ground
tasks.t: A Unitree Go1 quadruped on flat ground must follow a schedule of joystick velocity commands, covering forward, sideways and turning motion, for a whole episode without falling over. The commands change several times and it begins moving, so the legged robot has to track each new speed and direction closely and stay upright throughout.

tasks.n: Go1 follows joystick commands on rough ground
tasks.t: A Unitree Go1 quadruped on uneven ground with small bumps must follow a schedule of joystick velocity commands, covering forward, sideways and turning motion, for a whole episode without falling. The commands change many times, and the bumpy terrain makes foot placement and balance harder than on a flat floor.

tasks.n: Spot follows joystick commands
tasks.t: A Boston Dynamics Spot quadruped standing still on flat ground must follow a schedule of joystick velocity commands, covering forward, sideways and turning motion, for a whole episode without falling over. The commands change several times and sometimes drop to standing still, so the robot has to track each new demand and stay balanced.

tasks.n: Spot gets up after a fall
tasks.t: A Boston Dynamics Spot quadruped lies tipped over on the ground after being dropped from a height, with randomly bent legs. It must right itself and stand upright at its full normal height, and the stance has to be held briefly, which takes a controlled sequence of rolling, pushing and weight shifts.

tasks.n: Spot follows commands with a set gait
tasks.t: A Boston Dynamics Spot quadruped on flat ground must follow a schedule of joystick velocity commands for a whole episode without falling, while also stepping with a prescribed gait. The gait fixes which feet swing together, how fast they cycle and how high they lift, so the robot must match a rhythm as well as the speed and turning commands.

tasks.n: Sweep a blue brush forward
tasks.t: A KUKA iiwa 14 arm with a Sharpa HA4 dexterous hand must pick up a blue brush from a table and carry it through a long series of demonstrated goal poses in order, tracing a forward sweeping stroke over the table surface. A ghost copy of the brush marks the current goal, and the brush must match each pose closely, so the hand needs a secure tool grasp and smooth, accurate motion.

tasks.n: Swing a claw hammer downward
tasks.t: A KUKA iiwa 14 arm with a Sharpa HA4 dexterous hand must pick up a claw hammer from a table and carry it through a long series of demonstrated goal poses in order, reproducing a downward swing aimed at a nail prop. A ghost copy of the hammer marks the current goal, and because the tool's weight sits far from the hand the grasp has to stay firm through the swing.

tasks.n: Swing a claw hammer sideways
tasks.t: A KUKA iiwa 14 arm with a Sharpa HA4 dexterous hand must pick up a claw hammer from a table and carry it through a long series of demonstrated goal poses in order, reproducing a sideways swing aimed at a nail prop. A ghost copy of the hammer marks the current goal, and because the tool's weight sits far from the hand the grasp has to stay firm through the swing.

tasks.n: Flip something over with a flat spatula
tasks.t: A KUKA iiwa 14 arm with a Sharpa HA4 dexterous hand must pick up a flat spatula from a table and carry it through a long series of demonstrated goal poses in order, reproducing a flipping-over motion between bowl and plate props. A ghost copy of the spatula marks the current goal, so the grasp must stay steady while the flat blade is moved smoothly and accurately.

tasks.n: Serve onto a plate with a flat spatula
tasks.t: A KUKA iiwa 14 arm with a Sharpa HA4 dexterous hand must pick up a flat spatula from a table and carry it through a long series of demonstrated goal poses in order, reproducing a serving-onto-a-plate motion between bowl and plate props. A ghost copy of the spatula marks the current goal, so the grasp must stay steady while the flat blade is moved smoothly and accurately.

tasks.n: Wipe the letter C with an eraser
tasks.t: A KUKA iiwa 14 arm with a Sharpa HA4 dexterous hand must pick up a handle eraser from a table and carry it through a long series of demonstrated goal poses in order, wiping along the path of the letter C over a whiteboard prop. A ghost copy of the eraser marks the current goal, so the hand must hold the tool firmly and follow a curved path accurately.

tasks.n: Wipe a smiley face with an eraser
tasks.t: A KUKA iiwa 14 arm with a Sharpa HA4 dexterous hand must pick up a handle eraser from a table and carry it through a long series of demonstrated goal poses in order, wiping along the path of a smiley face over a whiteboard prop. A ghost copy of the eraser marks the current goal, so the hand must hold the tool firmly and follow a curved path accurately.

tasks.n: Spin a long screwdriver horizontally
tasks.t: A KUKA iiwa 14 arm with a Sharpa HA4 dexterous hand must pick up a long screwdriver from a table and carry it through a long series of demonstrated goal poses in order, spinning it about a horizontal axis. A ghost copy marks the current goal, and because the screwdriver must be turned while it stays in the hand, the motion needs in-hand reorientation and fine finger control rather than simple carrying.

tasks.n: Spin a long screwdriver vertically
tasks.t: A KUKA iiwa 14 arm with a Sharpa HA4 dexterous hand must pick up a long screwdriver from a table and carry it through a long series of demonstrated goal poses in order, spinning it about a vertical axis. A ghost copy marks the current goal, and because the screwdriver must be turned while it stays in the hand, the motion needs in-hand reorientation and fine finger control rather than simple carrying.

tasks.n: Swing a mallet downward
tasks.t: A KUKA iiwa 14 arm with a Sharpa HA4 dexterous hand must pick up a mallet hammer from a table and carry it through a long series of demonstrated goal poses in order, reproducing a downward swing aimed at a nail prop. A ghost copy of the mallet marks the current goal, and because the tool's weight sits far from the hand the grasp has to stay firm through the swing.

tasks.n: Swing a mallet sideways
tasks.t: A KUKA iiwa 14 arm with a Sharpa HA4 dexterous hand must pick up a mallet hammer from a table and carry it through a long series of demonstrated goal poses in order, reproducing a sideways swing aimed at a nail prop. A ghost copy of the mallet marks the current goal, and because the tool's weight sits far from the hand the grasp has to stay firm through the swing.

tasks.n: Sweep a red brush forward
tasks.t: A KUKA iiwa 14 arm with a Sharpa HA4 dexterous hand must pick up a red brush from a table and carry it through a long series of demonstrated goal poses in order, tracing a forward sweeping stroke over the table surface. A ghost copy of the brush marks the current goal, and the brush must match each pose closely, so the hand needs a secure tool grasp and smooth, accurate motion.

tasks.n: Sweep a red brush to the right
tasks.t: A KUKA iiwa 14 arm with a Sharpa HA4 dexterous hand must pick up a red brush from a table and carry it through a long series of demonstrated goal poses in order, tracing a sweeping stroke to the right over the table surface. A ghost copy of the brush marks the current goal, and the brush must match each pose closely, so the hand needs a secure tool grasp and smooth, accurate motion.

tasks.n: Draw a smiley face with a Sharpie
tasks.t: A KUKA iiwa 14 arm with a Sharpa HA4 dexterous hand must pick up a Sharpie marker from a table and carry it through a long series of demonstrated goal poses in order, drawing a smiley face on a whiteboard prop. A ghost copy of the marker marks the current goal, so the slim marker must be held securely and moved accurately along a curved path.

tasks.n: Write the letter C with a Sharpie
tasks.t: A KUKA iiwa 14 arm with a Sharpa HA4 dexterous hand must pick up a Sharpie marker from a table and carry it through a long series of demonstrated goal poses in order, writing the letter C on a whiteboard prop. A ghost copy of the marker marks the current goal, so the slim marker must be held securely and moved accurately along a curved path.

tasks.n: Spin a short screwdriver horizontally
tasks.t: A KUKA iiwa 14 arm with a Sharpa HA4 dexterous hand must pick up a short screwdriver from a table and carry it through a long series of demonstrated goal poses in order, spinning it about a horizontal axis. A ghost copy marks the current goal, and because the screwdriver must be turned while it stays in the hand, the motion needs in-hand reorientation and fine finger control rather than simple carrying.

tasks.n: Spin a short screwdriver vertically
tasks.t: A KUKA iiwa 14 arm with a Sharpa HA4 dexterous hand must pick up a short screwdriver from a table and carry it through a long series of demonstrated goal poses in order, spinning it about a vertical axis. A ghost copy marks the current goal, and because the screwdriver must be turned while it stays in the hand, the motion needs in-hand reorientation and fine finger control rather than simple carrying.

tasks.n: Flip something over with a spoon spatula
tasks.t: A KUKA iiwa 14 arm with a Sharpa HA4 dexterous hand must pick up a spoon spatula from a table and carry it through a long series of demonstrated goal poses in order, reproducing a flipping-over motion between bowl and plate props. A ghost copy of the spatula marks the current goal, so the grasp must stay steady while the blade is moved smoothly and accurately.

tasks.n: Serve onto a plate with a spoon spatula
tasks.t: A KUKA iiwa 14 arm with a Sharpa HA4 dexterous hand must pick up a spoon spatula from a table and carry it through a long series of demonstrated goal poses in order, reproducing a serving-onto-a-plate motion between bowl and plate props. A ghost copy of the spatula marks the current goal, so the grasp must stay steady while the blade is moved smoothly and accurately.

tasks.n: Draw a smiley face with a Staples marker
tasks.t: A KUKA iiwa 14 arm with a Sharpa HA4 dexterous hand must pick up a Staples marker from a table and carry it through a long series of demonstrated goal poses in order, drawing a smiley face on a whiteboard prop. A ghost copy of the marker marks the current goal, so the slim marker must be held securely and moved accurately along a curved path.

tasks.n: Write the letter C with a Staples marker
tasks.t: A KUKA iiwa 14 arm with a Sharpa HA4 dexterous hand must pick up a Staples marker from a table and carry it through a long series of demonstrated goal poses in order, writing the letter C on a whiteboard prop. A ghost copy of the marker marks the current goal, so the slim marker must be held securely and moved accurately along a curved path.

tasks.n: Hold a tray and insert a peg
tasks.t: Two Franka Panda arms, each with a four-finger Allegro hand, stand at a table where a tray with a round socket and a small round peg lie in front of them. One hand must hold the tray steady while the other picks up the peg and pushes it into the socket until it touches the bottom, so holding and fine insertion must be coordinated.

tasks.n: Rebuild a three-disk Tower of Hanoi
tasks.t: Two Franka Panda arms with Allegro hands face a wooden base with three posts in a row, each holding one disk of a different size, and must rebuild the full tower on the post at the right arm's side, largest disk at the bottom. A larger disk may never rest on a smaller one or on the table, so the disks must be moved in a carefully planned order.

tasks.n: Heat a hot dog in a microwave
tasks.t: Two Franka Panda arms with Allegro hands must open a microwave's hinged door, put a hot dog inside, shut the door again and press the start button, so that the food is inside, the door is closed and the button is pressed. The four subgoals depend on each other and have to happen in a forced order.

tasks.n: Take a photo with a held camera
tasks.t: Two Franka Panda arms with Allegro hands must pick up a camera lying on a table, hold it up in front of a logo disk at the far side so that it faces the logo, and press its shutter button with the other hand. The camera has to sit in the right region with the right aim while one hand holds it steady and the other presses.

tasks.n: Enter a passcode on an iPad
tasks.t: Two Franka Panda arms with Allegro hands must pick up an iPad resting on a stand and unlock it by touching the digits one, two and three in order with a fingertip, then keep it unlocked for a moment. Touching any wrong digit fails the episode, so the robot has to read the on-screen keypad and press single small buttons accurately.

tasks.n: Put a mouse on its pad and click
tasks.t: A single Franka Panda arm with a four-finger Allegro hand must move a computer mouse onto a round magenta mousepad and click its hinged button, which turns the monitor blue, then leave the mouse on the pad. A click made while the mouse is off the pad does nothing, so the order of moving and clicking matters.

tasks.n: Fold eyeglasses and put them in a case
tasks.t: A single Franka Panda arm with a four-finger Allegro hand must fold both hinged temples of a pair of eyeglasses lying open on a table and then place the folded glasses into the open case beside them. Folding two small hinges with one hand before the glasses can be moved takes fine finger control.

tasks.n: Drive a nail with a hammer
tasks.t: A single Franka Panda arm with a four-finger Allegro hand must pick up a hammer from the table and drive a nail into a wooden block by striking its head. A strike counts only if the hammer face is moving downward fast enough when it hits, so the arm must swing the tool with real momentum and aim accurately rather than just touching the nail.

tasks.n: Put boxed food in a bucket and lift it
tasks.t: A single Franka Panda arm with a four-finger Allegro hand must put a box of food into a bucket standing on the table and then lift the whole bucket clear of the table. The bucket has a hinged handle that swings freely, and both conditions are checked at the same moment, so the food must still be inside when the bucket is up.

tasks.n: Open and close kitchen tongs in the air
tasks.t: A single Franka Panda arm with a four-finger Allegro hand must pick up a pair of kitchen tongs from the table and, while holding them up in the air, open and close them several times by working their hinge. The same hand has to grip the tongs and squeeze them, so grasping and in-hand actuation must happen together.

tasks.n: Spray a potted plant with a spray bottle
tasks.t: A single Franka Panda arm with a four-finger Allegro hand must pick up a spray bottle, hold its nozzle near a potted plant while pointing it at the plant, and pull the trigger and keep it pulled for a short while. The trigger is a small hinge worked by the index and middle fingers, and pulling it while the nozzle is away from the plant fails, so aim and finger force both matter.

tasks.n: Reach a target with a muscle-driven arm
tasks.t: A musculoskeletal model of a human shoulder, arm and hand, hanging at its side and driven only by commands to its muscles, must bring its index fingertip to a small target sphere in front of the body and hold it there. With no joint controller, many muscles must be coordinated to reach a precise point in space.

tasks.n: Baoding balls in a muscle-driven hand
tasks.t: A musculoskeletal model of a human forearm and hand, palm up, holds two balls and must rotate them around each other so that each follows its own moving target marker as the targets circle the palm for a full orbit. The balls must not fall out, and the pair of moving targets demands continuous, finely coordinated finger muscle control.

tasks.n: Hand an object to a prosthetic hand
tasks.t: A musculoskeletal right arm and hand next to a motorized prosthetic left arm, standing at a table, must pick up an object with the biological hand, pass it to the prosthetic hand and set it on a goal pillar on the far side. It has to be held at each stage and must never touch the table or floor, so the exchange between two very different hands needs careful timing.

tasks.n: Chase and tag an opponent on foot
tasks.t: A free-standing musculoskeletal model of a human torso and both legs, driven by many leg muscles, must walk across a square arena to bring its pelvis close to an opponent standing in it, within a time limit. It must stay upright and inside the arena, so walking with muscle-level control is the main challenge, and in this instance the opponent does not move.

tasks.n: Fly a toy airplane along a recorded motion
tasks.t: A musculoskeletal model of a human forearm and hand starting at a pre-grasp pose must lift a toy airplane from a table and move it through the air so that its position and tilt follow a recorded human motion-capture reference. Matching a moving reference with an object in the grip demands a stable grasp and continuous finger control.

tasks.n: Lift an apple along a recorded motion
tasks.t: A musculoskeletal model of a human forearm and hand starting at a pre-grasp pose beside an apple on a table must lift the apple so that its path follows a recorded human motion-capture reference. The grasp has to hold a round object while it tracks a moving reference, using only muscle-level commands to the hand.

tasks.n: Lift and turn a bunny to inspect it
tasks.t: A musculoskeletal model of a human forearm and hand starting at a pre-grasp pose must lift a Stanford bunny figure from a table and turn it as if looking it over, so that its position and rotation follow a recorded human motion-capture reference. Orientation counts, so the grip must hold an irregular shape while it is rotated.

tasks.n: Lift and tilt a cup as if pouring
tasks.t: A musculoskeletal model of a human forearm and hand starting at a pre-grasp pose must lift a cup from a table and tilt it as if pouring, so that the cup's position and rotation follow a recorded human motion-capture reference. The grasp has to stay secure through the tilt while only muscle-level commands drive the hand.

tasks.n: Present a cylinder for a hand-over
tasks.t: A musculoskeletal model of a human forearm and hand starting at a pre-grasp pose must pick up a small cylinder from a table and present it as if offering it for a hand-over, so that the cylinder's path follows a recorded human motion-capture reference. The hand must keep a firm grip while tracking the reference.

tasks.n: Grasp and swing a hammer
tasks.t: A musculoskeletal model of a human forearm and hand starting at a pre-grasp pose must grasp a hammer lying on a table and swing it, so that its position and rotation follow a recorded human motion-capture reference. The heavy tool must be held firmly through a fast swing, and orientation counts as well as position.

tasks.n: Reorient a die in a muscle-driven hand
tasks.t: A musculoskeletal model of a human forearm and hand, palm up, holds a die and must rotate it in the hand until it matches the pose shown by a translucent target die, then keep it there for a moment. The die must not be dropped, and every turn has to be achieved with finger muscles alone.

tasks.n: Match a target hand pose
tasks.t: A musculoskeletal model of a human forearm and hand, starting in a rest posture, must curl its fingers, thumb and wrist into a given target pose, shown by translucent fingertip markers, and hold it for a moment. All of the joint angles have to be matched together through muscle commands rather than joint control.

tasks.n: Put all five fingertips on targets
tasks.t: A relaxed musculoskeletal model of a human forearm and hand must move the thumb and all four fingertips onto five small target spheres at once and hold them there for a moment. Five goals have to be reached together through muscle-level control, so the fingers must be coordinated to reach precise points in space.

tasks.n: Turn a key with a thumb-index pinch
tasks.t: A musculoskeletal model of a human forearm and hand has a key in a lock in front of the palm, with its head between thumb and index finger, and must turn the key by more than half a turn and hold it there. The turn needs a sustained pinch with fingertips that stay on the key head, driven only by muscle commands.

tasks.n: Hold an object in the palm
tasks.t: A musculoskeletal model of a human forearm and hand, palm up, has a small object resting in the palm and must keep the object at a goal point just above it for a moment. The object falls if the fingers do not grip it, so the hand has to close around it and hold it steady using muscle commands alone.

tasks.n: Reorient an object held in the hand
tasks.t: A musculoskeletal model of a human forearm and hand, palm up, has an object resting on its fingers and must turn it in the hand until its orientation matches a translucent target copy, then keep it there for a moment. The object is one of several possible shapes, and it must not be dropped while the fingers reposition it.

tasks.n: Run a track with a prosthetic leg
tasks.t: A free-standing musculoskeletal human model whose right leg is a motorised knee-and-ankle prosthesis must run forward along a straight flat track to the finish line, staying on its feet and near the centre line. Only the leg muscles are commanded, while the prosthesis runs its own controller, so a stable running gait has to be produced with a mixed biological and robotic body.

tasks.n: Twirl a pen to a target direction
tasks.t: A musculoskeletal model of a human forearm and hand, palm up, has a pen lying across its fingers and must rotate the pen in the hand until it points along the direction shown by a translucent target pen, then keep it there for a moment. The pen must not be dropped, and spinning a long thin object takes careful finger muscle coordination.

tasks.n: Place an object in a receptacle by hand
tasks.t: A musculoskeletal model of a human shoulder, arm and hand in front of a table must pick up an object standing on it and put it in a target receptacle, keeping it there for a moment. The whole arm and hand are driven by muscle commands, so reaching, grasping and carrying must all be coordinated without a joint controller.

tasks.n: Turn a key with weakened muscles
tasks.t: A musculoskeletal model of a human forearm and hand with muscles weakened to mimic age-related muscle loss has a key in a lock in front of the palm, and must turn the key by more than half a turn and hold it there. With every muscle at reduced strength, the sustained thumb-index pinch needed to turn the key is much harder to produce.

tasks.n: Score a goal past a goalkeeper
tasks.t: A free-standing musculoskeletal human model, with a very large number of leg muscles, stands on a soccer pitch with a ball in front of it and must kick the ball into the goal past a goalkeeper within a time limit. The kick must be hard enough to carry the ball to the goal while the body stays upright, which makes balance and striking power the main challenges.

tasks.n: Return a served table-tennis ball
tasks.t: A musculoskeletal model of a human torso, right arm and hand, on a pelvis that slides on the floor, holds a paddle at a table-tennis table and must return a served ball so that it lands on the opponent's half. The ball arrives quickly from the far side, so the model must watch its flight and hit it cleanly, using only muscle-level commands.

tasks.n: Spread a blanket flat on a table

tasks.n: Build an EKET cabinet frame from panels
tasks.t: On a table, two Franka Panda arms with two-finger hands must assemble an IKEA EKET cabinet frame: slide both side panels into the top panel, fit the back panel into its grooves, slide the bottom panel onto the sides, and leave the cabinet standing by itself. The panels join through mitres, keyholes and dowels with almost no slack, every joint has to be made in a fixed order, and grasps hold only by finger friction.

tasks.n: Assemble a GLADOM tray table with screws
tasks.t: Working with two Franka Panda arms with two-finger hands, the robot must build an IKEA GLADOM tray table: cross one leg frame into the other, drive the long and bottom screws, add the ring and fasten it with two more screws, then rest the loose tray on the ring. The small screws advance only when turned, using the hex driver that stands in the scene, and each step needs the previous parts seated and aligned.

tasks.n: Rebuild a serving stand and set its bowl
tasks.t: Here two Franka Panda arms with two-finger hands must rebuild an IKEA 365+ serving stand: unscrew the screw from one member and set it aside, lay the second member across the first, drive the screw back in through both, turn the stand over and place the bowl on it. The steps must happen in this order, the small screw is driven with a screwdriver from the scene, and the finished stand must rest firmly with its bowl.

tasks.n: Screw four legs onto a LACK table
tasks.t: Using two Franka Panda arms with two-finger hands, the robot must screw all four legs of an IKEA LACK side table onto the threaded studs of its tabletop, which lies studs up, one leg per stud, and let go with every leg seated. Each leg moves down only while it is being turned through several full revolutions, so the hands must grip it by friction alone, keep it on the thread and repeat this four times.

tasks.n: Build a STEGESUND roll stand with a hex key
tasks.t: With two Franka Panda arms with two-finger hands, the robot must build an IKEA STEGESUND roll stand: press the two leg halves together at their crossings, push the shelf in, drive four bolts into the shelf with a hex key, stand the frame upright and drop the top rod into its notches. The bolts turn only through the key seated in their sockets, and every part must end closely aligned with the frame.

tasks.n: Fit a lamp shade and screw in the bulb
tasks.t: Two ViperX arms of an ALOHA 2 robot must finish an IKEA SVALLET work lamp: push the shade's key down into the socket on top of the stand until a spring jaw snaps over it, then screw the bulb upward into the shade's socket until it seats. The snap needs a firm, well-aligned press, the bulb advances only by being turned, and the lamp must stay upright on the bench afterwards.

tasks.n: Assemble a VARIERA shelf insert with screws
tasks.t: At a bench, two Franka Panda arms with two-finger hands must assemble an IKEA VARIERA shelf insert: set the two side frames in place, lower the shelf onto them and drive four small screws through the shelf into the frames until their heads seat. The screws advance only when turned with the screwdriver provided in the scene, and nothing but the threads holds the parts together, so the frames must stay aligned throughout.

tasks.n: Snap together a VESKEN shelf unit
tasks.t: The task gives two Franka Panda arms with two-finger hands the parts of an IKEA VESKEN shelf unit to build: snap four feet into the bottom tray, then columns and trays level by level up to the top, and finally four caps into the top tray. All twenty-three snap connections must be made in that order, each pin pressed past a spring jaw and seated precisely, which makes this a very long, contact-heavy build.

tasks.t: A bimanual ALOHA 2 robot (two arms with parallel-jaw grippers) must pull apart two interlocked claw-shaped puzzle pieces and carry the brown one into a green dashed goal square, leaving the other on the puzzle side. Here the brown piece is a key and the other a teal lock. The pieces are locked with tight clearances, so freeing them takes a non-obvious sequence of rotations and slides, and the arms must coordinate. This instance is the medium variant.

tasks.n: Untie a knotted rope
tasks.t: A bimanual ALOHA 2 robot (two arms with parallel-jaw grippers) must untie a knotted rope lying on a table and spread it out until, seen from above, no part of it crosses or overlaps another, then let go of it. The rope is a long, floppy chain of segments, and the order in which crossings are removed matters, so the arms must plan the untangling as a small topology puzzle. This instance is the very easy variant.

tasks.t: A bimanual ALOHA 2 robot (two arms with parallel-jaw grippers) must untie a knotted rope on a table, one end clamped under a staple, and spread it with no crossings or overlaps seen from above, inside a goal rectangle, then let go. The rectangle appears only on marked-up camera images, not in the scene, and fixed posts and a curb stand nearby; removing crossings in the right order is a small topology puzzle. This instance is a medium variant.

tasks.n: Thread a key through rotor plates
tasks.t: A single Franka arm with a two-finger parallel gripper must pick up a two-tab key from its rest and push it through a stack of two jointed rotor plates and a final end plate, respecting their slots and stops. The key's leading tab is longer than the second, the clearances are tiny, and the tabs must line up with each plate's slot, so the key needs an ordered insert-and-rotate sequence.

tasks.n: Thread a key through rotor plates
tasks.t: A single Franka arm with a two-finger parallel gripper must pick up a two-tab key from its rest and push it through a stack of three jointed rotor plates and a final end plate, respecting their slots and stops. The key's leading tab is longer than the second, the clearances are tiny, and the tabs must line up with each plate's slot, so the key needs an ordered insert-and-rotate sequence.

tasks.t: A single Franka arm with a two-finger parallel gripper must pick up a two-tab key from its rest and push it through a stack of four jointed rotor plates and a final end plate, respecting their slots and stops. The key's leading tab is longer than the second, the clearances are tiny, and the tabs must line up with each plate's slot, so the key needs an ordered insert-and-rotate sequence.

tasks.n: Free a cord loop from an orbit puzzle
tasks.t: A bimanual ALOHA 2 robot (two arms with parallel-jaw grippers) must free a cord loop with a wooden handle from a fixed post and stopper ball and place the whole cord and handle inside a green dashed goal square, leaving the post, ball and base on the puzzle side. The cord is floppy and the loop has to be passed around the post and ball in a non-obvious order. This instance is the very easy variant.

tasks.n: Thread a rope through ordered rings
tasks.t: A bimanual ALOHA 2 robot (two arms with parallel-jaw grippers) must thread a rope through two rings picked out by colour (cyan then green), passing them in the stated order along the rope from one end to the other. The rope is floppy, the openings are identified only by colour, and the order and direction of each pass matter without adding extra crossings.

tasks.n: Thread a rope through ordered rings
tasks.t: A bimanual ALOHA 2 robot (two arms with parallel-jaw grippers) must thread a rope through three rings picked out by colour (cyan, green, then purple), passing them in the stated order along the rope from one end to the other. The rope is floppy, the openings are identified only by colour, and the order and direction of each pass matter without adding extra crossings.

tasks.n: Thread a rope through ordered rings
tasks.t: A bimanual ALOHA 2 robot (two arms with parallel-jaw grippers) must thread a rope through three rings picked out by colour (cyan, green, then purple), passing them in the stated order along the rope from one end to the other. The rope is floppy, the openings are identified only by colour, and the order and direction of each pass matter without adding extra crossings.

tasks.n: Thread a rope through ordered rings
tasks.t: A bimanual ALOHA 2 robot (two arms with parallel-jaw grippers) must thread a rope through four openings, two wall grommets and two rings, picked out by colour, passing them in the stated order along the rope from one end to the other. The rope is floppy, the openings are identified only by colour, and the order and direction of each pass matter without adding extra crossings. Longer chains of openings make the sequence harder to track.

tasks.t: A bimanual ALOHA 2 robot (two arms with parallel-jaw grippers) must thread a rope through four openings, two wall grommets and two rings, picked out by colour, passing them in the stated order along the rope from one end to the other. The rope is floppy, the openings are identified only by colour, and the order and direction of each pass matter without adding extra crossings. Longer chains of openings make the sequence harder to track.

tasks.n: Free a ring from a slotted post
tasks.t: A bimanual ALOHA 2 robot (two arms with parallel-jaw grippers) must free a removable metal ring threaded on a bendy cord with beads and end discs around a slotted post, and place the whole ring inside a green dashed goal square, leaving the post, cord, beads and discs on the puzzle side. The cord has to be worked around the slot in a non-obvious sequence before the ring comes free. This instance is the very easy variant.

tasks.n: Free a ring from a slotted post
tasks.t: A bimanual ALOHA 2 robot (two arms with parallel-jaw grippers) must free a removable metal ring threaded on a bendy cord with beads and end discs around a slotted post, and place the whole ring inside a green dashed goal square, leaving the post, cord, beads and discs on the puzzle side. The cord has to be worked around the slot in a non-obvious sequence before the ring comes free. This instance is an easier variant.
