The cord has to be worked around the slot in a non-obvious sequence before the ring comes free. This instance is the hard variant.

tasks.n: Align three blocks with a set square
tasks.t: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers, standing at a table, must use a triangular set square as a pushing tool to shove three cubes into one straight, neatly squared row without ever lifting a cube, then return to the home pose. Success depends on controlled sweeping contact with a held tool, because the cubes must end up on one line and turned the same way.

tasks.n: Arrange digit blocks into largest number
tasks.t: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers, at a table, must read the digits printed on four or five number blocks and place them one per mat along a row so that the digits, read in order, spell the largest possible number. The challenge is reading the digits from camera images and ranking them from largest to smallest before moving anything, then placing each block upright on its own mat.

tasks.n: Order digit blocks to largest number, cluttered
tasks.t: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers, at a table, must read the digits printed on four or five number blocks and place them one per mat along a row so that the digits spell the largest possible number. This randomised variant uses different object models and adds clutter around the blocks, so spotting and reading the right digits is harder before any ranking and placing begins.

tasks.n: Build a three-level wooden tower
tasks.t: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers, working at a table, must build a three-level tower from wooden blocks and boards: two pillars bridged by a long board, two more blocks and a second board above, then the top pieces. Each layer depends on the one below, so the order is fixed, and every piece must be placed accurately enough to stay stable and upright.

tasks.n: Sort small objects into three baskets
tasks.t: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers must sort the small objects on a table by category into three baskets, so that every item of one category lands in the same basket and each category gets its own. The categories are never named, so the robot has to work out from appearance which objects belong together, then carry out a long run of pick-and-place moves.

tasks.n: Sort objects into named baskets
tasks.t: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers, at a table, must follow a written instruction that names which kind of object goes into the left, middle and right basket, here cars, watches and wooden toys, and sort every object accordingly. It tests grounding category words in what the objects look like and then placing many items without mixing up the baskets.

tasks.n: Cover blocks with cups, then uncover in order
tasks.t: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers, at a table, must place three cups over three coloured blocks one after another from left to right, remembering which colour ended up under which cup, then lift the cups off one at a time in the order red, green, blue. The blocks are hidden once covered, so success needs memory plus a long, ordered sequence of cup moves.

tasks.n: Drop a coin into a piggy bank
tasks.t: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers, at a table, must lift a coin out of a vertical coin holder and drop it through the slot of a piggy bank, then return to the home pose. The coin is thin and stands in its holder, and the slot is narrow, so both the grasp and the alignment above the slot demand care.

tasks.n: Seat nuts on matching coloured bolts
tasks.t: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers, at a table, must pick up three nuts and fit each one onto the bolt of the same colour, leaving every nut upright and centred before the grippers let go. Matching nuts to bolts is done by colour and the fit is tight, so alignment has to be nearly exact for a nut to seat properly.

tasks.n: Move four eggs into a lidded holder
tasks.t: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers, at a table, must move four eggs one by one from a basket into the cups of an egg holder and then swing the holder's hinged lid shut. The eggs are rounded and easy to knock about, and the run ends with a hinge motion, so many pick-and-place moves must lead cleanly into the final closing.

tasks.n: Drop pens into a held pen holder
tasks.t: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers, at a table, must use one arm to steady a pen holder while the other arm drops four pens into it tip down, then set the holder back upright on the table. The two arms have different jobs at the same time, and the pens must go in the right way up without toppling the holder.

tasks.n: Fold a long-sleeve shirt
tasks.t: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers must fold a long-sleeved shirt lying flat on a table: first fold both sleeves in across the chest, then bring the bottom hem up to the shoulders, finishing with both arms back home and the grippers open. The cloth is simulated and deformable, the order of folds matters, and the robot works from camera images alone.

tasks.n: Fold a shirt in a cluttered scene
tasks.t: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers must fold a long-sleeved shirt lying flat on a table, first folding both sleeves in across the chest and then the bottom hem up to the shoulders. This randomised variant uses different object models and adds clutter, so the deformable cloth has to be handled with ordered folds while working only from camera images.

tasks.n: Lift a named object from clutter
tasks.t: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers, at a table, must pick up one object that is named only by a short description, for instance a mint green pair of scissors, from among a crowd of other items and lift it clear of the surface. The target comes from a wide pool of everyday object types, so the robot must recognise it by appearance and grasp very different shapes.

tasks.n: Hang three mugs on a rack
tasks.t: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers, at a table, must hang three mugs by their handles on the hooks of a mug rack, then return both arms home. The mugs start at varied angles, so the handle has to be located and hooked precisely onto the rack, which makes hanging an awkwardly oriented object the heart of the task.

tasks.n: Hang mugs on a rack amid clutter
tasks.t: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers, at a table, must hang three mugs by their handles on the hooks of a mug rack, then return home. This randomised variant uses different mug models and scatters many distractor objects over the table, so the robot must find each handle among clutter and still hook it precisely onto the rack.

tasks.n: Copy a demonstrated sorting order
tasks.t: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers watches a second, demonstrator arm put five objects into the far basket one after another, then must place its own matching copies into its basket in the same order. The order exists only in the live demonstration, so the robot has to remember it, match each item to its twin and keep its own arms out of the way while the other arm works.

tasks.n: Insert and turn a key
tasks.t: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers, at a table, must pick up a key, pass it from one gripper to the other, push it into a keyhole block and turn it so that it ends fully inserted, upright and rotated. It chains a handover, a tight insertion and a final twist, so alignment, depth and the turning motion all have to be right.

tasks.n: Insert test tubes into a rack
tasks.t: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers must pick up three test tubes lying on their sides on a table and push each one into a hole of a test-tube rack, then return home. The tubes start flat and must be stood upright, and the holes call for accurate alignment, so the robot needs a good grasp and a careful, precise insertion for each tube.

tasks.n: Declare a kong in mahjong
tasks.t: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers, at a table, must wait while an opponent arm discards a mahjong tile, then flip the three matching tiles in its own row and set an extra tile upright at the end of the row, with the grippers open. Which tiles to flip is known only after the discard, so the robot must watch, identify the matching face and then act.

tasks.n: Put bread in toaster and press lever
tasks.t: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers, at a table, must move two slices of bread from a bread rack into the two slots of a toaster, press the toaster lever down and return both arms home. The slices must go in upright and the lever needs a firm push, so the task chains pick-and-place, thin-slot insertion and a small mechanism.

tasks.n: Make toast amid clutter
tasks.t: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers, at a table, must move two slices of bread from a bread rack into the two slots of a toaster, press the toaster lever down and return both arms home. This randomised variant uses different object models and adds clutter, so the slices and the toaster must be located among distractors before the same chain of placing and pressing.

tasks.n: Pick the matching object off a conveyor
tasks.t: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers watches a moving belt: the first object to appear is the one to remember, and when an identical object comes past again among decoys the robot must pick it off the belt and lift it. Items keep arriving over time, so the target has to be recognised from memory and grasped while it is moving.

tasks.n: Tidy a desk with four items
tasks.t: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers must tidy a desk by setting an alarm clock on a drawer unit, a figurine on its stand and a mouse on a mouse pad, and by pushing a keyboard into its frame, then go home. Four unrelated items each have their own destination, so the robot mixes lifting with a pushing action and must pick the right place for each one.

tasks.n: Pack four items into a box facing left
tasks.t: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers, at a table, must put a toy car, an electric toothbrush, a hammer and a shoe into a box so that every item points the same way, to the left, and the box ends up upright and aligned. The four items differ widely in shape, so the robot must work out each front from its appearance and fit them all in under the orientation rule.

tasks.n: Pack four items into a box, cluttered
tasks.t: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers, at a table, must put a toy car, an electric toothbrush, a hammer and a shoe into a box so that every item points to the left and the box ends up upright and aligned. This randomised variant uses different object models and adds clutter, so each item and its front have to be picked out of a busier scene.

tasks.n: Pick conveyor target shown in a photo
tasks.t: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers must look at a photo on a board to learn which of four objects riding a conveyor is the target, pick it up, put it in a basket and lift the basket with the target inside. The belt carries the items along, so the robot must match the photo to the right object, track it while it moves and grasp it in time.

tasks.n: Load stacking-toy pieces onto four pegs
tasks.t: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers, at a table, must put all ten pieces of a stacking toy onto the four pegs of its base, each piece centred on its peg, then return home. The pieces fall into uneven groups and the text never says which group belongs on which peg, so the robot has to infer it from the pieces' models and sizes, then place ten parts accurately.

tasks.n: Play tic-tac-toe against an arm
tasks.t: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers plays tic-tac-toe as first player against a second, opponent arm, taking turns placing pieces on a board until it is full. The opponent puts its pieces on random empty squares, so the robot must wait for each move, see where it went and choose among the remaining squares, while keeping its own arms clear whenever the opponent arm is moving.

tasks.n: Play a xylophone with a mallet
tasks.t: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers, at a table, must pick up a mallet from its stand and strike the keys of a xylophone one after another from left to right, lifting the mallet clear of the keys between strikes. It is a tool-use task with a repeated strike pattern, where aim and strike height must stay consistent along the whole row.

tasks.n: Plug a charger into a power strip
tasks.t: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers, at a table, must pick up a charger plug and push it fully into a socket on a power strip so that it sits upright, then return home. Plug and socket start in varied places on either side of the table and the fit is tight, so position and angle must be lined up before pushing in.

tasks.n: Pour balls from a cup into a vase
tasks.t: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers, at a table, must pick up a cup holding several small balls, tip it over a vase until every ball has dropped in, set the cup back upright and return home. The balls roll freely, so the pour has to be aimed at the vase mouth and tilted carefully, and the cup must be put down cleanly afterwards.

tasks.n: Pour bottles into bowls as instructed
tasks.t: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers must follow a written sentence that names which bottle to pour into which bowl, with bottles and bowls identified by their order and colour, and carry out the pours in the stated order. The liquid is simulated, pouring out of order ends the attempt, and the robot must ground the words in the right bottles and bowls from camera views.

tasks.n: Pour a bottle into a cup
tasks.t: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers must pick up a bottle, tip it so that simulated liquid pours into a cup, and then stand the bottle upright again. Nearly all of the liquid has to land in the cup and not on the table, so the tilt and the position of the spout over the cup matter, as does righting the bottle at the end.

tasks.n: Pour a bottle into a cup, cluttered
tasks.t: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers must pick up a bottle, tip it so that simulated liquid pours into a cup, and then stand the bottle upright again. This randomised variant uses different object models and adds clutter, so the bottle and cup are harder to pick out, while almost all of the liquid still has to land in the cup.

tasks.n: Press buttons by number cards
tasks.t: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers, at a table, must read two number cards and press the first red button as many times as the first card says, then the blue button, then the second red button as many times as the second card says, then blue again. Counting presses exactly matters, since one press too many ends the attempt, so the robot must read digits and keep an accurate count.

tasks.n: Push a T block onto its pad
tasks.t: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers, at a table, must push a T-shaped block across the surface, without lifting it, until it lies exactly on a gray T-shaped pad with the same position and orientation. The block slides and rotates under the gripper, so many small corrections are needed to match both where it sits and which way it points.

tasks.n: Push a T block onto its pad, cluttered
tasks.t: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers, at a table, must push a T-shaped block, without lifting it, until it lies exactly on a gray T-shaped pad with the same position and orientation. This randomised variant uses different object models and fills the table with many distractor objects, so the sliding path has to be planned around clutter while the final fit stays tight.

tasks.n: Put four bottles into a dustbin
tasks.t: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers must pick up four bottles, some standing and some lying, and put them into a raised dustbin beside the table, using a handover between the arms when a bottle is out of reach of one arm. The dustbin sits off to the side, so the task needs reach planning and passing bottles between the grippers.

tasks.n: Complete an arithmetic equation with a tile
tasks.t: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers sees an arithmetic equation laid out on pads with exactly one digit or operator missing, and must pick the right tile from the loose tiles on the table and place it on the empty pad. It needs reading digits and operators from images, working out the missing value, and then a clean placement among distractor tiles.

tasks.n: Line up nesting dolls by size
tasks.t: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers, at a table, must stand five nesting dolls upright in a straight row ordered from the smallest to the largest. The dolls start scattered in random order, so the robot has to judge relative size from images and place each doll in the correct slot of the row.

tasks.n: Line up nesting dolls by size, cluttered
tasks.t: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers, at a table, must stand five nesting dolls upright in a straight row ordered from the smallest to the largest. This randomised variant uses different doll models and adds clutter, so the dolls must be found among distractors and ranked by visual size before each goes into its slot.

tasks.n: Stack three blocks into a tower
tasks.t: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers, at a table, must stack three blocks that differ only in texture into a single tower, in any order, then return home. It is a basic stacking test: each block has to be set down accurately enough to stay balanced on the one below, with the order left free.

tasks.n: Stack cubes in a named colour order
tasks.t: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers, at a table, must stack three differently coloured cubes into a tower following a written instruction that gives the colour order from bottom to top, here blue, then yellow, then orange. The robot must match the colour words to the cubes it sees and respect the order while stacking accurately.

tasks.n: Stack three blocks amid clutter
tasks.t: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers, at a table, must stack three blocks that differ only in texture into a single tower, in any order, then return home. This randomised variant uses different object models and scatters many distractor objects over the table, so the right blocks have to be found among clutter before the careful stacking.

tasks.n: Nest three identical bowls
tasks.t: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers, at a table, must nest three identical bowls into a single stack, then return home. The bowls look alike, so the challenge is lowering each one squarely into the one below, since curved, rimmed bowls can tilt or slide when released a little off position.

tasks.n: Nest three bowls among clutter
tasks.t: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers must nest three identical bowls into a single stack on a table and then bring both arms back to their starting pose. Many unrelated objects are scattered around as distractors, and the bowl and clutter models come from a randomised variant, so the task tests handling unfamiliar items in a messy scene.

tasks.n: Hang headphones, close and rack laptop
tasks.t: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers must hang a set of headphones on their stand, shut a laptop that starts open, and then stand the closed laptop upright in a vertical storage rack before returning to the start pose. It is a chain of three different manipulations, including a hinged lid and a thin object that has to be placed on its edge.

tasks.n: Store laptop and headphones amid clutter
tasks.t: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers must hang a set of headphones on their stand, close an open laptop, and place the closed laptop upright in a vertical rack, then return to the start pose. Laptop and headphone models are randomised and many distractor objects crowd the table, so the long chain of steps must succeed in a messier, less familiar scene.

tasks.n: Place four tools in matching slots
tasks.t: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers must put a hammer, pliers, a tape measure and a wrench each into its own matching slot in a toolbox, in the correct orientation, and then return to the start pose. The tools start split between the left and right sides of the table, so each must be recognised by shape and set down so that it actually fits its slot.

tasks.n: Swap two cubes using a spare mat
tasks.t: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers must swap the places of two cubes sitting on a row of three mats, using the empty third mat as a temporary parking spot, and press a spring button after each of the three moves. It is a small planning puzzle with a strict order of moves and presses, so the arms must keep track of what has already been done.

tasks.n: Swap two T-shaped blocks
tasks.t: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers must pick up two T-shaped blocks lying on a table, exchange their places, and set each down at the position and heading the other one had, then return to the start pose. The blocks begin at arbitrary angles, so the arms must remember both starting poses and reproduce them accurately.

tasks.n: Hand over broom and sweep cubes
tasks.t: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers must pick up a broom, pass it to the right arm, and use it with a dustpan that stays on the table to sweep a handful of small cubes into the dustpan before returning to the start pose. It combines a handover with tool use, and pushing loose cubes needs steady, sustained contact.

tasks.n: Sweep mixed small items into dustpan
tasks.t: A pair of ARX X5 arms with two-finger grippers must pick up a broom, hand it to the right arm, and use it with a stationary dustpan to sweep a random mix of small bricks, earbuds and paper balls into the dustpan, then return to the start pose. The items to sweep differ in shape and size, so the sweeping motion must collect all of them.

tasks.n: Relay a ball between two cups
tasks.t: Two Franka Panda arms, each carrying a square cup, must relay a ball that is thrown up at the start: the left cup catches it and tosses it to the right cup, which carries it on and throws it back, and the left cup finally delivers it into a box sliding to and fro on a rail. Everything moves from the first moment, with mid-air catches and a moving final target.

tasks.n: Strike, catch and merge two balls
tasks.t: Two Franka Panda arms, one with a flat paddle and one with a cup, face two inclined lanes that release balls on their own at different moments. The paddle must touch each ball once it is flying free, while the cup catches the first ball, carries it away, catches the second while still holding the first, and finally drops both into a fixed basin to rest.

tasks.n: Hit a puck through gaps in turns
tasks.t: Two Franka Panda arms, each holding a paddle, must take turns hitting one low-friction puck that is already sliding when the episode starts: left, right, left, right. The first three hits must send it through different gaps in a row of posts between the arms and the last must drive it over a goal line, so each return has to be watched to place and time the next strike.

tasks.n: Carry a tray with a loose ball together
tasks.t: Two Franka Panda arms, each with a small fork cradling one end of a tray that holds a loose ball, must carry the tray together through two waypoints that form a turn, calm the ball after the environment pushes it, and then tip it out into a fixed basin. The ball may not leave the tray early and the tray may not drop, so both arms must move in careful step.

tasks.n: Relay a ball through a held channel
tasks.t: Two Franka Panda arms face off: the left holds a cup with a ball in it and the right holds a straight, open-ended channel. The left arm passes the ball into the channel and catches it in flight as it leaves the far end, then repeats the relay with the channel held at a clearly different angle and finally delivers the ball into a fixed basin.

tasks.n: Bank a puck off a rebound board
tasks.t: Two Franka Panda arms with paddles play a bank-shot game: the right paddle hits a low-friction puck that is already sliding in through a gap in a row of posts, and the left paddle acts as a rebound board that sends it back through the same gap. After a second strike and a rebound through the other gap with the board repositioned, the puck must cross a goal line untouched by the right paddle.

tasks.n: Swing a gate while shooting a puck
tasks.t: Two Franka Panda arms work around a low-friction puck in a U-shaped pen of bouncy rails: the left arm grips a spring-loaded swinging gate with its bare gripper while the right paddle drives the puck into the pen. The gate must be swung the opposite way at the moment the puck hits a side rail, after which the puck is intercepted and shot across a goal line with the gate still deflected.

tasks.n: Swing and settle a pendulum together
tasks.t: Two Franka Panda arms, each holding a flat paddle, stand either side of a passive pendulum, a rod with a ball-shaped bob. The left paddle must push it into a swing, the right paddle must meet and brake it and then drive it back, and the left paddle touches it once more, after which the pendulum must hang almost straight down and nearly still.

tasks.n: Launch, catch and reload a ball
tasks.t: Two Franka Panda arms share a see-saw launcher: the right arm uses its cup to load a ball into the launcher's basket, the left arm strikes the lever with a mallet to fling the ball into the air, and the right cup catches it. The cycle is repeated, and the ball must finally come to rest in a box sliding on a rail, without the mallet ever touching it.

tasks.n: Hand over a part from a moving conveyor
tasks.t: Two Franka Panda arms with plain grippers must take a long bar-shaped part off a running roller conveyor, the left arm grasping it while it moves and lifting it. The left arm then presents it for a hand-over, with both grippers briefly holding it, and the right arm lays it into a long open slot sliding back and forth on a rail.
st: part held by the left gripper

tasks.n: Unlock a moving fixture to release a ball
tasks.t: Two Franka Panda arms must free a ball from a hand-held fixture: the left arm grips the fixture and lifts it off its stand, and while it is still moving the right arm inserts a peg into a socket, presses a latch button until a gate opens, and withdraws. The ball then runs down a fixed chute into a basin, and the fixture must never be dropped.

tasks.n: Slide a cube between two scoops
tasks.t: Two Franka Panda arms each hold a level, shallow scoop that is open toward the other, and a cube on a very slippery surface starts on the left scoop. Without tilting, the arms must accelerate so that the cube slides onto the right scoop and back, then set it on a fixed output platform at rest, so the cube is moved by inertia and kept in contact with the scoops.

tasks.n: Flip a cube twice on a tray
tasks.t: Two Franka Panda arms, the left holding a large shallow tray bearing a cube and the right a small flat pusher, must flip the cube over twice so that its original bottom face ends up on top. Each flip is a short push that ends before the cube is half way over, leaving it to complete the tip on its own momentum, and the tray finally carries the cube to an output point.

tasks.n: Catch a ball and route it into a cart
tasks.t: A single Franka Panda arm holding an open cup must catch a ball thrown up at the start, pour it into the designated one of two raised channels, then catch it again in flight after it rolls out and bounces off a tilted plate. It finally puts the ball in a cart sliding along a rail, so timing against two flights and a moving target is critical.

tasks.n: Catch and carry a ball on a plate
tasks.t: A single Franka Panda arm holding a flat plate with no rim must catch a ball tossed up at the start, settle it at the plate's centre, carry it through two waypoints that make a turn without it rolling off, and finally tip it into a basin sliding back and forth along a rail. Balancing a rolling ball on a flat surface and releasing it into a moving target are the difficulties.

tasks.n: Clear a blocker and bank a puck home
tasks.t: A single Franka Panda arm with a paddle must strike a puck sliding toward it over an almost frictionless table so that it hits a sliding blocker bar and shoves it aside along its rail. After the puck returns, a second strike must bank it off the long side rail and across the goal line while the blocker is still pushed aside, so both hits need real force and timing.

tasks.n: Strike a block to release a ball
tasks.t: A single Franka Panda arm with a paddle must strike a small block sliding toward it along a raised deck so that it hits a spring-held latch and swings a gate open, setting free a ball on an inclined chute. The paddle then intercepts the rolling ball, sends it through a narrow passage between two walls, and brings it to rest in a target zone.

tasks.n: Receive a sliding cube and move it by inertia
tasks.t: A single Franka Panda arm holding a shallow tray open on one side must receive a cube sliding off a slippery lane, then, without tilting the tray, make the cube slide inside it to a staging point just by accelerating. After carrying it through two waypoints, the arm must match the speed of a platform sliding on a rail and get the cube onto it without touching it.

tasks.n: Flip a cube and slide it to a pocket
tasks.t: A single Franka Panda arm with a pusher blade must tip a cube resting on a raised surface so that the face initially toward the robot ends on top, the blade letting go so the cube completes the flip on its own momentum. The blade then pushes the cube onto an inclined chute, meets it near the lower end, and brings it to rest in a pocket with the same face still up.

tasks.n: Move a part from conveyor to dock via carriage
tasks.t: A single Franka Panda arm with a gripper must grasp a small part riding a running conveyor, set it on a carriage that is already coasting along a rail, then grab the carriage's vertical handle to stop it with the part still aboard. It finally regrasps the part and sets it in a fixed dock, so almost everything happens on moving objects.

tasks.n: Load a cart, throw the switch, recover the part
tasks.t: A single Franka Panda arm with a gripper must grasp a small part riding a conveyor, drop it into a cart coasting along a channel, and push a hinged track switch with a finger so that the cart is steered into the branch chosen for this instance. It then grasps the part again and lifts it out of the cart before the cart runs too far, which demands careful timing.

tasks.n: Catch, self-toss and recatch a ball
tasks.t: A single Franka Panda arm holding a shallow cup with one open side must catch a ball thrown high at the start, then toss it straight up out of the cup with a genuine throw and catch it again after moving the cup sideways. It finally releases the ball into a box sliding along a rail, where it must settle while the box is moving.

tasks.n: Carry a swinging load past an obstacle
tasks.t: A single Franka Panda arm must grip a short carrier bar with a pendulum already swinging beneath it and damp the swing by timing its own motion against it. It then carries the bar through two waypoints without letting the bar or pendulum touch a block, damps the leftover swing again, and lowers the bar until the pendulum's ball rests centred in a dock.

tasks.n: Rescue a rolling cylinder and deliver it
tasks.t: A single Franka Panda arm holding a tray open on one side must intercept a short cylinder rolling off the end of a raised lane and bring it to rest lying along a required direction. It then sends the cylinder through a gently sloping guide channel without touching it, catches it again at the exit, and delivers it with the same alignment into a pocket sliding on a rail.

tasks.n: Send a puck across a spinning bridge
tasks.t: A single Franka Panda arm with a paddle must strike a puck sliding along a raised lane so that it crosses a platform spinning continuously about a vertical axis and reaches an exit lane. The paddle then intercepts it, strikes it again and sends it past a hinged, partly open gate and over a goal line without touching it as it crosses and with the gate still open.

tasks.n: Close a dishwasher and its racks
tasks.t: A Unitree G1 humanoid with two-finger grippers must push two pulled-out racks into a dishwasher and then shut its open door. The three parts depend on each other, since both racks have to be in before the door can close, and the humanoid must do it while its whole-body controller keeps it upright.

tasks.n: Load plates into a dishwasher rack
tasks.t: A Unitree G1 humanoid with two-finger grippers must take two plates from a dish rack on the counter and stand them on edge in the lower rack of an open dishwasher, then let go so that both stay standing without help. Slotting thin plates upright and gently, without dropping any, makes this a delicate placement task.

tasks.n: Open the top kitchen drawer
tasks.t: A Unitree G1 humanoid with two-finger grippers must open the top drawer of a kitchen cabinet by pulling it nearly all the way out. It is a single articulated-object pull, but the humanoid must grip the drawer and pull steadily while its whole-body controller keeps it balanced.

tasks.n: Turn an upside-down cup upright
tasks.t: A Unitree G1 humanoid with two-finger grippers must turn an upside-down cup the right way up and gently set it back down on the counter. The cup has to be grasped, rotated through a half turn and released upright, so it is a small reorientation task that depends on careful grasping.

tasks.n: Flip a spoon in a mug
tasks.t: A Unitree G1 humanoid with two-finger grippers must lift a spoon out of a mug, turn it end over end and put it back into the same mug, which stays where it is. Flipping a utensil with two-finger grippers calls for a careful regrasp, and the spoon then has to be returned into the mug's opening.

tasks.n: Move two plates between dish racks
tasks.t: A Unitree G1 humanoid with two-finger grippers must take both plates out of the left dish rack and stand them on edge in the slots of the right dish rack, facing right. Both plates must be standing in the right rack at the same time, so the humanoid has to carry each one across and slot it in gently without knocking anything over.

tasks.n: Carry a box to the kitchen counter
tasks.t: A Unitree G1 humanoid with two-finger grippers must pick a cardboard box up from a low side table and set it gently down on the kitchen counter. The box has noticeable weight and must be lifted from low to counter height, so the load shifts the humanoid's balance and its whole-body controller is stressed.

tasks.n: Put cups away in a wall cabinet
tasks.t: A Unitree G1 humanoid with two-finger grippers must take two cups from the counter and put them away on the bottom shelf of a wall cabinet. The glass doors start closed, so the humanoid has to open a door first and then place the cups one after the other, three dependent steps in sequence.

tasks.n: Touch two target spheres with both hands
tasks.t: A Unitree G1 humanoid with two-finger grippers must touch a red sphere with its left hand and a green sphere with its right hand at the same time. The spheres are placed ahead of the robot, one to each side, and both hands must reach their own target together while the legs and waist stay balanced.

tasks.n: Slide a sandwich off a pan with a spatula
tasks.t: A Unitree G1 humanoid with two-finger grippers must use a spatula to move a sandwich from a frying pan onto a chopping board and leave it lying flat. The task fails if a gripper touches the sandwich, so the humanoid has to wield the tool and slide the food across without dropping it.

tasks.n: Move a saucepan from cabinet to hob
tasks.t: A Unitree G1 humanoid with two-finger grippers must take a saucepan out of an under-counter cabinet and set it gently on the hob. The cabinet door starts closed, so the humanoid first has to open it down low, then lift out the pan and carry it up to the cooking surface.

tasks.n: Stack three blocks on a pad
tasks.t: A Unitree G1 humanoid with two-finger grippers must move three blocks to a second table and stack them on a green pad. Each block has to sit on the previous one, so the placements depend on each other, and the humanoid must carry the blocks between tables before it can build a stable tower.

tasks.n: Open both doors of a wall cabinet
tasks.t: A Unitree G1 humanoid with two-finger grippers must swing both hinged doors of a wall-mounted cabinet wide open. Both doors have to end up open together, which means reaching up to the high cabinet and handling two hinged panels with the gripper fingers while staying balanced.

tasks.n: Hand over a mug and hang it on a tree
tasks.t: A pair of I2RT YAM arms with two-finger grippers at a workstation table must pick up a mug with the left arm, pass it in mid-air to the right arm, and hang it on a mug tree, with both grippers letting go at the end. The in-air handover and the placement onto a slender tree make this a coordinated, contact-rich sequence, and each instance uses a different mug and tree shape.

tasks.n: Carry a pot onto a cooktop
tasks.t: A pair of I2RT YAM arms with two-finger grippers at a workstation table must lift a pot with both grippers holding it, set it down upright on a cooktop and let go. Both arms have to share the load and move together, and the pot must end up resting stably and level on the small cooktop rather than tilted or dropped. Each instance uses a different pot and cooktop shape.

tasks.n: Open drawer and place bowl, bowl moves
tasks.t: A single Franka Panda arm must pull open the top drawer of a wooden cabinet and then put a black bowl inside it. As the gripper first approaches the bowl, the bowl is nudged a little across the table, so a plan fixed from the first frame misses and the arm must re-aim its grasp before carrying the bowl to the opened drawer.

tasks.n: Bowl on stove, bowl moves
tasks.t: A single Franka Panda arm must pick up a black bowl and place it on a stove. As the gripper first approaches the bowl, the bowl is shifted sideways across the table, so a plan fixed from the first frame misses and the arm must re-aim its grasp before setting the bowl down on the stove.

tasks.n: Bowl on plate, plate moves
tasks.t: A single Franka Panda arm must pick up a black bowl and put it on a plate. As the gripper first approaches the bowl, the plate jumps a short distance diagonally across the table, so a plan fixed from the first frame misses its target and the arm must re-locate the plate before placing the bowl.

tasks.n: Bowl on cabinet top, obstacle appears
tasks.t: A single Franka Panda arm must pick up a black bowl and place it on top of a wooden cabinet. As the gripper first approaches the bowl, a block of cream cheese appears right beside it as an obstacle, so the approach and grasp must be re-planned around the newcomer before the bowl is carried up to the cabinet top.

tasks.n: Cream cheese on bowl, obstacle appears
tasks.t: A single Franka Panda arm must pick up a box of cream cheese and put it on top of a black bowl. As the gripper first approaches the cheese, a wine bottle appears right beside it as an obstacle, so the grasp must be re-planned around the bottle and the cheese placed accurately on the bowl.

tasks.n: Turn off stove, colours change
tasks.t: A single Franka Panda arm must switch off a stove by turning its knob back past the off point. As the gripper first approaches the stove, the camera image colours are scrambled, so the arm must still locate the stove and turn its knob even though everything looks different from before.

tasks.n: Turn on stove, lighting dims
tasks.t: A single Franka Panda arm must switch on a stove by turning its knob far enough to count as on. As the gripper first approaches the stove, the scene lighting drops to a fraction of its brightness, so the arm must find and turn the knob in a much darker view.

tasks.n: Turn on stove, lighting dims
tasks.t: A single Franka Panda arm must switch on a stove by turning its knob far enough to count as on; this instance words the instruction slightly differently. As the gripper first approaches the stove, the scene lighting drops to a fraction of its brightness, so the arm must find and turn the knob in a much darker view.

tasks.n: Turn on stove, camera noise
tasks.t: A single Franka Panda arm must switch on a stove by turning its knob far enough to count as on. As the gripper first approaches the stove, the camera images suddenly become noisy and part of the view is blocked, so the arm must find and turn the knob from degraded visual input.

tasks.n: Wine bottle on plate, plate moves
tasks.t: A single Franka Panda arm must pick up a wine bottle and put it on a plate. As the gripper first approaches the bottle, the plate jumps a short distance diagonally across the table, so a plan fixed from the first frame misses its target and the arm must re-locate the plate before placing the bottle.

tasks.n: Wine bottle on rack, camera shift
tasks.t: A single Franka Panda arm must pick up a wine bottle and set it on a wine rack on the table. As the gripper first approaches the bottle, the camera viewpoint moves, tilts and zooms differently, so the placement has to be completed from a changed view of the scene.

tasks.n: Wine bottle on rack, obstacle appears
tasks.t: A single Franka Panda arm must pick up a wine bottle and set it on a wine rack on the table. As the gripper first approaches the bottle, a black bowl appears right beside it as an obstacle, so the approach and grasp must be re-planned around the newcomer before the bottle is placed on the rack.

tasks.n: Wine bottle on rack, colours change
tasks.t: A single Franka Panda arm must pick up a wine bottle and set it on a wine rack on the table. As the gripper first approaches the bottle, the camera image colours are scrambled, so the arm must still recognise the bottle and the rack even though everything looks different from before.

tasks.n: Wine bottle on cabinet top, camera noise
tasks.t: A single Franka Panda arm must pick up a wine bottle and place it on top of a wooden cabinet. As the gripper first approaches the bottle, the camera images suddenly become heavily noisy and a large part of the view is blocked, so the pick and the placement must be finished from badly degraded visual input.

tasks.n: Turn on stove, camera shift
tasks.t: A single Franka Panda arm must switch on a stove by turning its knob far enough to count as on. As the gripper first approaches the stove, the camera viewpoint moves, tilts and zooms differently, so the arm must find and turn the knob from a changed view of the scene.

tasks.n: Soup and cheese into basket, basket moves
tasks.t: A single Franka Panda arm must put both an alphabet soup and a cream cheese box into a basket, finding the two named groceries among other packages on the table. As the gripper first approaches the soup, the basket jumps a short way across the table, so a plan fixed from the first frame would miss it and the arm must adapt.

tasks.t: A single Franka Panda arm must put a black bowl into the bottom drawer of a wooden cabinet and then push the drawer closed. As the gripper first approaches the bowl, a wine bottle appears as an obstacle on a different side of the bowl than in the sibling instance, so the approach must be re-planned, and the drawer has to end fully shut.

tasks.n: Two mugs to plates, camera shift
tasks.t: A single Franka Panda arm must put a white mug on the left plate and a yellow-and-white mug on the right plate, with left and right taken as seen when facing the robot across the table. Mid-task, as the gripper first closes in on the first mug, the camera viewpoint shifts and tilts, so the mugs must still be told apart by colour and sent to the correct plates from a changed view.

tasks.n: Mug and pudding by plate, camera noise
tasks.t: A single Franka Panda arm must put a white mug on a plate and place a chocolate pudding to the right of that plate, choosing the correct mug over a second one. tasks.n: Alpine Slalom
tasks.t: Ski the slalom: one run down the course on your skis, both ski tips and both feet through each of the 32 gates in order, then over the finish line.

tasks.n: Standing backflip and landing
tasks.t: A Unitree G1 humanoid standing in the middle of an empty, flat exercise floor must do a standing backflip: jump, rotate backwards through a full turn in the air, land on its feet and stand up. The whole rotation has to come from a single brief flight launched from a standing start, so the task needs a powerful, well-timed take-off and a controlled landing without falling.

tasks.n: Badminton Serve
tasks.t: Serve: standing in your right service court, let the shuttle go from your left hand and hit it with the racket in your right hand, base first and below 1.15 m, over the net into the receiver's service court diagonally opposite.

tasks.n: Walk the balance beam
tasks.t: A Unitree G1 humanoid starts standing in a one-foot-in-front-of-the-other stance on the near end of a raised gymnastics balance beam and must walk along it to the far end and stand there without anything touching the floor. The beam is narrower than the robot's normal stance, so ordinary walking would put the feet beside it and the gait needs careful balance.

tasks.n: Stay balanced on a roller board
tasks.t: A Unitree G1 humanoid stands with its feet on a deck that rests on a free-rolling roller and must stay balanced there for a sustained period, with neither end of the deck nor any part of the robot touching the floor. The starting pose is an unstable equilibrium that would run out within seconds if left alone, so continuous corrective control is needed.

tasks.n: Dribble a basketball up the court
tasks.t: A Unitree H1-2 humanoid on a basketball court must dribble a ball with its right hand from the end line across the centre line, walking the whole way without a dribbling or travelling violation. The ball must be repeatedly pushed to the floor and met again on its bounce while the robot keeps walking, so hand timing and gait have to work together.

tasks.n: Bowl a strike
tasks.t: A Unitree H1-2 humanoid stands behind the foul line of a bowling lane with a ball hanging from its right hand and must deliver it down the lane so that all ten pins are knocked down. The pins are very far away, so the ball must be released with enough speed and on a straight line, and the release timing sets both its pace and direction.

tasks.n: Jump onto a plyometric box
tasks.t: A Unitree H1-2 humanoid standing in front of a tall plyometric box must jump onto it from a two-foot take-off, land on top with both feet and stand up straight. The box rests loose on the floor and can slide or tip if pushed, and a slow, quasi-static motion cannot leave the ground, so the jump needs real take-off power and a stable landing.

tasks.n: Punch a heavy bag
tasks.t: A Unitree H1-2 humanoid facing a hanging heavy bag must punch it once with the knuckles of its right fist on a marked band, hard enough to give it a required push, then bring the fist back to guard and stand. A shove or slap does not count, so the task needs a short, fast blow with good aim and a controlled recovery.

tasks.n: Breaking Windmill
tasks.t: Breaking: go down to the floor and do three consecutive windmills, rolling over your upper back, shoulders and chest while your legs circle round above the floor.

tasks.n: Catch a fly ball
tasks.t: A Unitree H1-2 humanoid standing on a level field must catch a baseball that is launched from far away and comes down steeply near it, gripping the ball with a hand before it touches the ground or the body and holding on. The landing spot is not fixed, so the robot has to observe the flight and get a hand there in time.

tasks.n: Catch a pass and shoot
tasks.t: A Unitree H1-2 humanoid at the top of the key of a basketball court must catch a chest pass thrown to it from the left wing and then shoot from where it stands so that the ball drops into the basket from above. It combines receiving a fast, moving ball with an accurate throw, and the incoming pass has to be observed to place the catch.

tasks.n: Clean and jerk a barbell
tasks.t: A Unitree H1-2 humanoid standing over a barbell on a lifting platform must lift it to its shoulders, then to locked arms overhead, and hold it motionless there until the down signal. The weight is too heavy for the arm joints alone, so the lift depends on driving with the legs and keeping balance under a heavy load.

tasks.n: Crawl under low wires
tasks.t: A Unitree G1 humanoid starting upright must get down under a course of low wires strung lower than its hips, and crawl the whole length until its entire body is past the last wire, without touching any wire. It must change from walking to a prone crawl and then keep its body low and clear of a long series of wires.

tasks.n: Throw a discus from the circle
tasks.t: A Unitree H1-2 humanoid inside a throwing circle must throw the discus held in its right hand so that it lands inside the marked sector at a required minimum distance, then leave the circle through its rear half and stand. It needs a fast whole-body throw while staying inside the circle, and a release that sends the discus the right way.

tasks.n: Dodgeball
tasks.t: Dodge: five cloth dodgeballs are thrown at you by ball machines that aim at you; do not let a live ball touch you, stay inside your court and on your feet.

tasks.n: Double Dutch
tasks.t: Jump Double Dutch: enter the two ropes turning in opposite directions and jump them 10 times in a row, one rope per jump, without a rope ever touching you, then land on your feet.

tasks.n: Dribble a football through slalom
tasks.t: A Unitree G1 humanoid on a grass pitch must dribble a football out through a line of six cones, round the last one and back through them over the start line, keeping the ball close and touching no cone. Each cone must be passed on the side shown by a mark, and the ball must be tapped and met again as it rolls free.

tasks.n: Jump and dunk a basketball
tasks.t: A Unitree H1-2 humanoid standing under a basketball hoop with the ball in its right hand must jump, force the ball down through the ring from above with its hand on it, and land on its feet. The ring is higher than the robot can normally reach, so the jump needs real take-off power and a controlled landing.

tasks.n: Dunk Between Legs
tasks.t: From the top of the key, with the basketball held in your two hands, dribble it, make one of its bounces pass between your legs, gather it in both hands, and with at most two steps dunk it: force it down through the ring from above with your hands on it, then land on your feet.

tasks.n: First Time Shot
tasks.t: Shoot first time: the football rolls down a ramp and across in front of you; with one touch of a foot send it into the official goal 11 m away.

tasks.n: Free Kick Wall
tasks.t: Take a direct free kick: with one kick of a foot, send the ball over or around the wall of mannequins into the official goal 20.0 m away.

tasks.n: Shoot a basketball free throw
tasks.t: A Unitree H1-2 humanoid standing just behind the free-throw line of a basketball court must throw the ball held in its right hand so that it enters the basket from above. A shot that drops through the ring needs the ball to leave the hand at the right speed and angle, so the task is mainly about a precise, repeatable throwing motion while staying balanced.

tasks.n: Freeski 360
tasks.t: Drop in from the start platform, ride the in-run, take off from the kicker, do a 360 in the air, land on your skis and ride away past the finish line.

tasks.n: Freeski Straight Air
tasks.t: Drop in from the start platform, ride the in-run, take off from the kicker, do a straight air in the air, land on your skis and ride away past the finish line.

tasks.n: Giant Slalom
tasks.t: Ski the giant slalom: one run down the course on your skis, both ski tips and both feet through each of the 26 gates in order, then over the finish line.

tasks.n: Goalkeeper Save
tasks.t: Keep goal: three penalty kicks are shot at the official goal you stand in; keep every ball out, with a foot on the goal line at each kick.

tasks.n: Sink a golf putt
tasks.t: A Unitree G1 humanoid standing side-on on a putting green must hole a putt of a few metres, using one stroke of a putter held in its right hand to roll a golf ball across in front of its feet into the hole. The putter strike has to be a brief tap with the right speed and direction, since a push or a second stroke does not count.

tasks.n: Handstand
tasks.t: Do a handstand: from your stance get up onto your hands, hold the handstand still for 2 s with only your hands on the floor, then come back down onto your feet and stand.

tasks.n: Head a crossed football into goal
tasks.t: A Unitree H1-2 humanoid standing at the edge of the goal area must meet a football crossed from the wing with its head and send it into the goal past a goalkeeper dummy. The ball arrives at head height from the side after a delay, so the robot has to watch its flight, time a whole-body lunge, and use its head as the striking surface.

tasks.n: Giant swing on the high bar
tasks.t: A Unitree G1 humanoid hanging by both hands from a gymnastics high bar must perform one giant swing, taking its extended body in a full circle around the bar without letting go. Nothing holds the legs up, so the swing must be built up from below the bar with whole-body momentum and carried over the top while the grip holds.

tasks.n: Run up and clear the high jump
tasks.t: A Unitree H1-2 humanoid starts well back on a runway and must approach a high-jump bar, take off from one foot, go over the bar between the uprights without knocking it off, and come down on the landing mat. It combines a running approach with a powerful one-foot take-off, and a quasi-static motion cannot leave the ground.

tasks.n: Hurdles Freestanding
tasks.t: Run the 50 m hurdles over four free-standing hurdles: go over each one in your lane, never beside it, under its top, or after pushing it away, leave at least one of them standing, and bring your torso to the finish line.

tasks.n: Inline Slalom
tasks.t: Skate the speed slalom: from the start box, 12 m of run-up, then on one foot through the 20 cones, passing them alternately left and right, and over the end line, as fast as you can.

tasks.n: Throw a javelin over the shoulder
tasks.t: A Unitree H1-2 humanoid on a javelin runway must throw the javelin held in its right hand over the shoulder so that its head strikes the ground first, inside the marked sector at a required distance, then leave the runway behind the arc and stand. It needs a powerful whole-body throw with the right release timing, while staying behind the throwing line.

tasks.n: Juggle three balls in a cascade
tasks.t: A Unitree G1 humanoid standing on level ground with a ball resting on each forearm must juggle three balls in a cascade, throwing each ball in an arc from one hand to the other and catching it, until a long run of catches has been made without a drop. All three balls are in the air at once, so the throws and catches must keep a steady rhythm.

tasks.n: Keep a football up with feet
tasks.t: A Unitree G1 humanoid standing on grass must drop a football from its hand and keep it in the air for a run of consecutive touches using its feet, legs or head, without letting it reach the ground or touch a hand again. Each touch must be an active strike that sends the ball back up, so the robot has to balance, sometimes on one foot, while placing the ball.

tasks.n: Juggling Feet
tasks.t: Juggle the football with your feet: drop it from between your palms and keep it in the air for ten foot touches in a row, each one sending the ball up above your knees, without it touching the ground or any other part of you.

tasks.n: Juggling Head
tasks.t: Juggle the football on your head: a ball machine in front of you lobs it onto your head; keep it in the air with ten headers in a row, touching it with nothing but your head, without it touching the ground.

tasks.n: Jump Rope
tasks.t: Skip rope: turn the rope forwards with both hands, over your head and under your feet, and jump it with both feet together, 17 times within one minute.

tasks.n: Kick a heavy bag
tasks.t: A Unitree H1-2 humanoid stands in front of a hanging heavy bag and must deliver one hard kick with its right foot or shin onto a marked band at trunk height, then settle back onto both feet. The blow has to be sharp and short rather than a slow push, which demands balancing on one leg while swinging the other.

tasks.n: Make a basketball layup
tasks.t: A Unitree H1-2 humanoid holds a basketball in its right hand inside the restricted area of a basketball court and must take a couple of steps toward the basket, jump, and let the ball go in the air close to the ring so it drops in from above. The steps are limited and the release must happen mid-flight, so run-up, take-off and release have to be timed together.

tasks.n: Long jump into a sand pit
tasks.t: A Unitree G1 humanoid starts far back on a runway and must run up, take off from behind the take-off line, fly over the gap beyond it and land inside the sand pit. The jump must be a real flight rather than a fall, the takeoff may not overstep the line, and the landing on soft sand must stay stable.

tasks.n: Long Rope
tasks.t: Jump the long rope: standing in the middle of a rope turned by two rope-turning machines, jump it 10 times in a row, the rope passing under both your feet while you are in the air, without the rope ever touching you.

tasks.n: Keep a ball bouncing on a paddle
tasks.t: A Unitree G1 humanoid with a table tennis paddle fixed to its right hand must keep a dropped table tennis ball bouncing on the paddle for a long run of consecutive bounces, each one returning the ball to about the height it fell from. Every bounce is an active upward hit, so the robot has to watch the ball and place the paddle precisely each time.

tasks.n: Take a penalty kick past the keeper
tasks.t: A Unitree G1 humanoid stands a few steps behind the penalty mark and must walk up and kick the football into the goal with a single kick, past a goalkeeper dummy that slides sideways to cut off the shot. Beating the keeper takes a fast, well-aimed strike rather than a gentle push, all while balancing on the standing leg.

tasks.n: Pitch a baseball for a strike
tasks.t: A Unitree H1-2 humanoid stands on a pitcher's mound with a baseball in its right hand and must throw it, in the air all the way, through the strike zone above home plate far ahead. The throw needs a fast, accurately aimed release from the hand while the body stays on the plate, so speed and aim must be coordinated.

tasks.n: Platform 10M
tasks.t: Do a forward dive straight (101A) from the 10 m platform: from your standing start at its front end, take off, turn half a somersault forwards in the straight position and enter the water head first, vertical, with your arms stretched beyond your head.

tasks.n: Pole vault over a bar
tasks.t: A Unitree H1-2 humanoid carries a rigid pole down a runway and must plant its tip in the box, swing off the ground hanging on it, clear the bar between the uprights without knocking it down, and come down on the mat. Without enough run-up momentum from the plant the robot never leaves the ground, so a long, fast sequence of phases has to be timed together.

tasks.n: Round Off
tasks.t: Do a round-off: go from your feet onto your hands, turn half round through the handstand and come down onto both feet together facing back the way you came, then stand.

tasks.n: Rugby Conversion
tasks.t: Kick a conversion: with one place kick of a foot, send the rugby ball standing on its tee over the crossbar and between the posts.

tasks.n: Put a shot from a circle
tasks.t: A Unitree H1-2 humanoid stands in a throwing circle with a heavy shot held at its neck and must push it from the shoulder with one hand so it lands inside the marked sector at a good distance, then step out of the circle through its rear half and stand. The shot is heavy and must be put rather than slung, so the whole body has to contribute while the hand stays in the legal position.

tasks.n: Run a four-leg shuttle
tasks.t: A Unitree G1 humanoid stands behind a start line on a sports floor and must run to a far line and back, twice over, planting a foot beyond the line at each turn, as fast as it can. The qualifying time is below what a walking gait reaches, so the robot has to run and make quick, stable turns without falling.

tasks.n: Skateboard Ollie
tasks.t: Ollie the skateboard from a standstill: pop the tail, take the board up with your feet until all of it is at least 0.05 m off the ground, land on it and stand still on it for 1.0 s.

tasks.n: Run an agility course round cones
tasks.t: A Unitree G1 humanoid starts beside the start cone of an agility course and must run the prescribed route: around the far corner cones, back to the start line, weaving up and down through the four centre cones, and across the finish, without touching a cone. The route is a sequence of gates passed on given sides, and the time limit forces running with sharp turns instead of a walk.

tasks.n: Sled Push
tasks.t: Push the weighted sled with your palms on its two upright handles until the whole sled is over the line 12.5 m ahead, within 60 s.

tasks.n: Snowboard
tasks.t: Ride the parallel slalom on your snowboard: one run down the course, the board and both feet through each of the 18 gates in order, then over the finish line.

tasks.n: Springboard 3M
tasks.t: Do a forward dive straight (101A) from the 3 m springboard: from your standing start at its end, take off from both feet, turn half a somersault forwards in the straight position and enter the water head first, vertical, with your arms stretched beyond your head.

tasks.n: Sprint a short race on the starter's lamp
tasks.t: A Unitree G1 humanoid waits in its lane at the start line of a short running track and must sprint straight down the lane until its torso crosses the finish line. The starter's gun is replaced by a lamp that turns red, yellow, then green, so the robot must watch it and leave only on green, and the qualifying time requires running rather than walking.

tasks.n: Standing long jump from a line
tasks.t: A Unitree G1 humanoid stands with its feet just behind a take-off line and must jump forward off both feet without a step, land at least its own height beyond the line, and then stay standing. The jump needs a genuine flight phase from a standstill, and the landing is judged by the nearest contact, so a stumble or a hand put down shortens the jump.

tasks.n: Clear a hurdle and water pit
tasks.t: A Unitree H1-2 humanoid starts on a track and must run up to a hip-high steeplechase hurdle, get over it and the dry water pit behind it, climb out beyond the pit's far edge and finish standing. The sequence of obstacles needs a long stride and a controlled landing on the sloping pit floor, with no stumbling.

tasks.n: Sumo
tasks.t: Win a sumo bout: force the opponent robot out of the ring, or make any part of it other than its feet touch the ground, before the same happens to you.

tasks.n: Sweeper Jump
tasks.t: Jump the sweeper: standing on your podium, jump over the padded boom each time it sweeps round, 3 times in a row without being hit, then stand still on the podium.

tasks.n: Return a table tennis serve
tasks.t: A Unitree G1 humanoid stands at one end of a table with a paddle on its right hand and must hit a served table tennis ball, after its first bounce on the robot's side, so that it lands on the opponent's side. The ball is within reach for only a very short moment and arrives with spin, so it must be tracked after the bounce and met with a timed swing.

tasks.n: Taekwondo Kick
tasks.t: Kick the trunk protector of the dummy in front of you once with a foot, hard enough to score, then land and stand still for 2.0 s.

tasks.n: Return a tennis serve
tasks.t: A Unitree H1-2 humanoid waits as the receiver on a tennis court with a racket on its right hand and must hit a served ball, after it bounces in the service box, back over the net into the far singles court. The return calls for a powerful, timed swing, and the robot has to read the serve's bounce and move a few metres sideways to get to the ball in time.

tasks.n: Serve a tennis ball into the box
tasks.t: A Unitree H1-2 humanoid stands behind the baseline of a tennis court with a ball in its left hand and a racket on its right and must toss the ball, hit it before it lands, and send it over the net into the diagonally opposite service box. Only one serve is allowed, and even the gentlest legal serve needs a fast racket swing timed to the falling toss.

tasks.n: Hanging toes-to-bar repetitions
tasks.t: A Unitree G1 humanoid hangs from a high horizontal bar by both hands and must repeatedly swing its feet up to touch the bar between its hands and return to a full hang each time, without letting go. Nothing holds the legs up, so the swinging legs and arms must be coordinated to repeat the movement several times.

tasks.n: Trampoline
tasks.t: On the trampoline, bounce as you like, then do one tuck jump, land on both feet, stop the bounce (one more straight out-bounce at most) and stand still.

tasks.n: Trap a rolling football
tasks.t: A Unitree H1-2 humanoid stands on grass while a football is passed along the ground past it and must stop the ball with a foot on first touch, bringing it to rest close to itself within a few moments. A still foot would just send the ball away, so the foot has to yield at the right instant while the robot balances on one leg, and the pass must be tracked as it arrives.

tasks.n: Triple jump into a sand pit
tasks.t: A Unitree G1 humanoid starts far back on a runway and must run up, hop from behind the take-off line landing on the same foot, step onto the other foot, and jump from it into the sand pit. Three separate flights are required, with only the supporting foot touching down between them, so each take-off and landing must be controlled to avoid sliding or falling.

tasks.n: Vault over a gymnastics table
tasks.t: A Unitree H1-2 humanoid starts at the end of a long run-up and must run to a springboard, vault over a shoulder-high vault table touching it only with its hands, land on its feet on the mat and stand. The robot needs run-up momentum to flip its body over the table, and the board moves on a spring, so contact, flight and landing must all be timed.

tasks.n: Vertical jump to touch a vane
tasks.t: A Unitree G1 humanoid stands under a measuring stand and must jump straight up off both feet from a standstill, touch the vane above it with a hand at the top of the jump, then land on its feet and stay standing. The jump has to leave the floor for a real flight without any step, and the hand must reach high enough at the right moment.

tasks.n: Volley a crossed ball into goal
tasks.t: A Unitree H1-2 humanoid stands at the penalty mark while a football is crossed in from the wing and must strike it with a foot before it touches the ground, sending it into the goal past a goalkeeper dummy. The ball comes in steeply from the side and must leave faster than it arrived, so the kick must be aimed and timed on a flying ball while balancing on the other leg.

tasks.n: Receive a volleyball serve
tasks.t: A Unitree H1-2 humanoid stands in a volleyball court while an opposing serve comes over the net and must pass it with its forearms in a single short contact, sending it above net height into the setter's target at the net. The serve is a floating ball that falls steeply to one side, so the robot has to track it and get its forearms underneath at the right moment.

tasks.n: Toss and serve a volleyball
tasks.t: A Unitree H1-2 humanoid stands behind the end line of a volleyball court with the ball on its left fist and must toss it, then hit it with one hand or arm over the net into the opponent's court. The ball has to be clear of the robot before the hit and the toss may not be a throw, so the hit must be timed to a falling ball and carry it far enough.

tasks.n: Set a volleyball for a hitter
tasks.t: A Unitree H1-2 humanoid stands near the net of a volleyball court while a tossed ball comes down above it and must set it with a single overhead contact of its hands, sending it more than a metre above the net into the outside hitter's target along the net. The contact must be brief and above the head, and the ball's arrival has to be observed to place the hands correctly.

tasks.n: Jump and spike a volleyball
tasks.t: A Unitree H1-2 humanoid stands at the attack line of a volleyball court while a set ball comes down near the net and must jump and hit it with a hand above net height, driving it down into the opponent's court, then land on its feet without touching the net. The jump has to be timed to the falling ball, and the strike must point downward, not just forward.

tasks.n: Throw at a wall target and catch
tasks.t: A Unitree H1-2 humanoid stands behind a line facing a wall with a tennis ball in its right hand and must throw the ball at a target circle on the wall, then catch the rebound with a hand before it touches the ground and keep hold of it. The throw must be fast and accurate, and the catch needs the hand in the right place when the ball returns.

tasks.n: Badminton duel against learned opponent
tasks.t: A Franka Panda arm with a racket, mounted on a sliding gantry, plays a singles badminton game on a scaled-down court against a built-in opponent driven by a learned policy. The player sees only camera images and the game runs slowed down, while the opponent reads the true shuttle state, so each return needs quick perception and a well-timed stroke.

tasks.n: Badminton match against scripted opponent
tasks.t: A Franka Panda arm with a racket, mounted on a sliding gantry, plays a singles badminton game on a scaled-down court against the strongest tier of scripted opponent, which reacts faster, recovers more quickly after each stroke and attacks harder more often. The game runs in slowed real time with only camera images, so each return demands quick tracking and well-timed hits.

tasks.n: Epee fencing bout against scripted fencer
tasks.t: Two Unitree G1 humanoids with real epees fence a direct-elimination bout, played out one short phrase at a time. For each phrase the player picks a tactical intention such as a lunge, a counter-attack or a retreat, against a stronger scripted fencer of the second level that reads those choices. The player works from camera images and has to plan a whole bout rather than a single exchange.

tasks.n: Foosball match against scripted opponent
tasks.t: A motorised foosball table with four rods for one team, driven by slide and rotation commands, plays a game against a scripted computer team of the third level under tournament rules. The player sees the table only through an overhead camera and the game runs in slowed real time, so the program must track a fast ball, time its shots, and respect limits on how long a rod may hold the ball.

tasks.n: Two-a-side humanoid soccer match
tasks.t: An agent commands two Booster T1 humanoids as a team in a soccer match against a scripted opposing team on a small boarded pitch, trying to score more goals over two halves. The robots see only through their head cameras, so the ball, teammates, opponents and goals must be told apart visually, and the game keeps running while the agent thinks, pausing only briefly after each point for a review.

tasks.n: Wheeled robot soccer match
tasks.t: An agent commands a team of five small omnidirectional wheeled soccer robots against an opposing team on a Small Size League field, trying to score more goals over two halves. It sees the game through shared overhead cameras with a delay and issues move, kick and dribble commands, so passing, shooting and defending must be planned in real time. In this instance the opponent is a stronger team whose robots are steered by a learned network.

tasks.n: Table tennis duel against a learned player
tasks.t: A Franka Panda arm with a paddle, mounted on a rail so it can slide along the end of the table, plays a table tennis game against a built-in opponent robot that uses a learned policy. Only camera images and the arm's own state are available, and play is slowed but never waits, so the agent must track the fast ball, return it, and review the game between points.

tasks.n: Table tennis match against a scripted opponent
tasks.t: A Franka Panda arm with a paddle, mounted on a rail behind the table end, plays a table tennis game against a scripted opponent. Only camera images and the arm's own state are available, and play is slowed but never waits, so the agent must track the fast ball, return it and serve legally. In this instance the opponent is a strong high-level player, and the match must be started within a limited window.

tasks.n: Fetch can from cabinet to top
tasks.t: A hovering hexarotor drone with a small arm and gripper must get a soda can out of a tall cabinet and leave it resting on top. The can starts hidden in a compartment behind a closed sliding door, so the drone must slide the door open, reach in, grasp the can, pull it out and lift it, and the can has to settle rather than keep moving.

tasks.n: Harvest a lemon into a tote
tasks.t: A hovering hexarotor drone with a small arm and gripper must pull a lemon off a wall and drop it into an open tote on a small table beside the wall. The lemon is held by a breakable joint among six limes that are fixed in place, so the drone must tell the fruits apart, tear the right one free and release it over the tote.

tasks.n: Fly to a wall inspection point
tasks.t: A hovering hexarotor drone with a small arm starts outside a large warehouse and must fly up the outer wall to an inspection point in front of a rectangle marked with hazard tape, then hold the arm's tip there. The point is far above the start, beyond the arm's reach and outside the cameras' initial view, so the task is as much about flight and navigation as about holding position.

tasks.n: Swing open a hinged door
tasks.t: A hovering hexarotor drone with a small arm and gripper faces a free-standing door in a metal frame and must swing the hinged oak panel open, away from itself, by a clear angle. The panel is held only by hinge damping and friction, and the lever handle is purely visual, so there is nothing solid to grab and the drone has to push on the panel itself.

tasks.n: Insert a held peg into socket
tasks.t: A hovering hexarotor drone with a small arm starts out gripping a metal peg and must push its tip into a square socket mounted on a wall ahead, until it sits well inside the opening. The wall can lean and the opening may leave little clearance, so the drone has to line the peg up precisely in both position and orientation.

tasks.n: Press a wall-mounted push button
tasks.t: A hovering hexarotor drone with a small arm and gripper must press a round, spring-loaded button on a wall in front of it far enough for the plunger to count as pushed in. The plunger has only a short travel and springs back when released, so the drone has to push straight into the wall and keep pushing while staying steady in the air.

tasks.n: Raise a spring-loaded wall lever
tasks.t: A hovering hexarotor drone with a small arm and gripper must swing a lever on a wall upward from its straight-out rest position by a good angle. The lever is spring-loaded and strongly damped, so it creeps back toward rest once released, and the drone has to drive it well up and keep it there while staying steady in the air.

tasks.n: Push a slider knob along its rail
tasks.t: A hovering hexarotor drone with a small arm and gripper must push a red knob along a long horizontal rail on a wall, from one end almost to the other. The knob stays where it is left but resists with friction and damping, so the drone must keep up a steady push over the whole sweep while it hovers in front of the wall.

tasks.n: Turn a wall valve wheel
tasks.t: A hovering hexarotor drone with a small arm and gripper must turn a large red valve wheel on a wall clockwise through a large part of a turn, using the handle bar that sticks out of the wheel's face. The wheel has no end stops and only damping and friction, and the handle sits off the axis, so the drone must push it around an arc while staying steady in the air.

tasks.n: Insert
tasks.t: Move the 50 mL centrifuge tube from the rack it stands in to the other rack, into the slot at row 0, column 4 (AutoBio's indices: s.task.rack2.get_position(s.data, 0, 4, '50ml')). Success at the first control step where the tube's body is within 15 mm (horizontally) of that slot's centre and its height is between 0.829 and 0.831 m (standing in a slot it is at 0.830 m).

tasks.t: Load a second 1.5 mL tube into the centrifuge's rotor, into the slot diametrically opposite the tube that is already in it (slot 8 of 30, s.task.slot_id; the tube in the rotor is in slot 23). The tube to load stands in the plate on the bench. Success at the first control step where the tube's body is within 5 mm of its seated position in that slot (s.task.final_tar_tubepose) and its height is between 0.955 and 0.961…

tasks.n: Pickup
tasks.t: Pick up the 50 mL centrifuge tube that stands in the rack. Success, at the first control step where both hold: the tube's body is above z = 0.925 m (it stands at 0.830 m, so 9.5 cm up) and the gripper's left finger (geom 1/aloha:leftfinger) touches the tube's cap (geom 1/cap_cyl).

tasks.t: Aspirate from the 50 mL centrifuge tube with the pipette. AutoBio's test is a sequence: (1) with the plunger pressed (the thumb's target, action entry arm1_dh_rh_thj3, above 0.70 rad), the pipette tip is within 6.5 mm (horizontally) of the tube's axis and more than 5 mm below the liquid surface; (2) the plunger is released (the thumb's target below 0.45 rad) while the tip is still below the surface; (3) success at…

tasks.n: Screw Loose
tasks.t: Unscrew the cap of the 50 mL centrifuge tube and lift it off. Success at the first control step where the cap is more than 0.15 m above the tube body's origin (screwed on it sits 0.1197 m above it, so 3 cm up), arm1's left finger (geom 1/aloha:leftfinger) touches the cap (geom 6/cap_cyl), and the cap's thread (geom 6/nut) no longer touches the tube's (geom 7/bolt).

tasks.n: Screw Tighten
tasks.t: Screw the cap onto the 50 mL centrifuge tube. The tube stands open in the rack; its cap lies on the bench. Success at the first control step where the cap is less than 0.123 m above the tube body's origin (fully screwed on: 0.1197 m), the cap's axis is within 5 mm of the tube's, and the cap's thread (geom 6/nut) touches the tube's (geom 7/bolt).

tasks.n: Thermal Cycler Close
tasks.t: Close the lid of the thermal cycler and lock it. Success at the first control step where the lid's hinge (/thermal_cycler_biorad_c1000:lid) is within 0.01 rad of -1.9 rad (fully closed; it starts open, at 0) and the lid's lever (/thermal_cycler_biorad_c1000:lid-lever) is within 0.01 rad of -0.94 rad (the locked end of its travel; it starts at 0).

tasks.n: Thermal Cycler Open
tasks.t: Open the lid of the thermal cycler. It starts closed and locked: the lid's hinge (/thermal_cycler_biorad_c1000:lid) at -1.9 rad and its lever (/thermal_cycler_biorad_c1000:lid-lever) at -0.94 rad. Success at the first control step where both are within 0.003 rad of 0 (fully open).
